title.zh: 卷一百二十四 載記第二十四 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲
title.en: Volume 124 Records 24: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 載記第二十四 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲 Volume 124 Records 24: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun

sentences.zh: 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲

translations.literal: Murong Bao, Murong Sheng, Murong Xi, Murong Yun
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun

sentences.zh: 慕容寶，字道祐，垂之第四子也。

translations.literal: Murong Bao, courtesy name Daoyou, was the fourth son of Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao, whose courtesy name was Daoyou, was the fourth son of Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 少輕果無志操，好人佞己。

translations.literal: In youth he was frivolous and rash, without resolve or principle, and fond of those who flattered him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was reckless and impulsive, lacking firm purpose, and he delighted in sycophants who played to his vanity.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時為太子洗馬、萬年令。

translations.literal: Under Fu Jian he served as Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household and Magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he held the posts of Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household and Magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 堅淮肥之役，以寶為陵江將軍。

translations.literal: In Jian's campaign at the Huai and Fei rivers, Bao was made General Who Crosses the River.
translations.idiomatic: During Fu Jian's campaign on the Huai and Fei, Bao was appointed General Who Crosses the River.

sentences.zh: 及為太子，砥礪自修，敦崇儒學，工談論，善屬文，曲事垂左右小臣，以求美譽。

translations.literal: When he became heir apparent, he sharpened himself in self-cultivation, deeply honored Confucian learning, was skilled in discourse and good at literary composition, and curried favor with the petty officials at Chui's side to seek a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Once made heir apparent, he applied himself to self-improvement, earnestly promoted Confucian learning, was adept at debate and polished at composition, and assiduously courted the minor officials around Murong Chui in hope of a glowing reputation.

sentences.zh: 垂之朝士翕然稱之，垂亦以為克保家業，甚賢之。

translations.literal: The courtiers of Chui's reign uniformly praised him, and Chui too thought he could preserve the family enterprise and greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chui's courtiers united in praising him, and Chui himself believed he would safeguard the family legacy and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 垂死，其年寶嗣偽位，大赦境內，改元為永康。

translations.literal: When Chui died, that same year Bao succeeded to the usurped throne, proclaimed a general amnesty within the realm, and changed the reign title to Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: The year Murong Chui died, Bao took the throne in his stead, declared a general amnesty throughout the realm, and adopted the reign title Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 以其太尉庫辱官偉為太師、左光祿大夫，段崇為太保，其餘拜授各有差。

translations.literal: He made his Grand Commandant Kurou Guan Wei Grand Preceptor and Left Household Counselor of the Imperial Clan, Duan Chong Grand Mentor, and the rest received appointments each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his Grand Commandant Kurou Guan Wei Grand Preceptor and Left Household Counselor of the Imperial Clan, made Duan Chong Grand Mentor, and assigned the remaining offices at various ranks.

sentences.zh: 遵垂遺令，校閱戶口，罷諸軍營分屬郡縣，定士族舊籍，明其官儀，而法峻政嚴，上下離德，百姓思亂者十室而九焉。

translations.literal: Following Chui's dying instructions, he reviewed household registers, abolished the various military camps and assigned their men to counties and commanderies, fixed the old registers of the gentry clans, and clarified their official ceremonies — yet the laws were severe and government harsh; superiors and inferiors were estranged in virtue, and of every ten households nine had minds set on rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In accordance with Chui's last testament he audited household registers, dissolved the military encampments and reassigned their troops to local counties, restored the old gentry registers and clarified official protocol — yet his laws were harsh and his rule severe; court and people alike fell out of accord, and rebellion was on the minds of nine households in ten.

sentences.zh: 初，垂以寶塚嗣未建，每憂之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Bao had not yet established an heir in the main line, Chui had worried about it constantly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Murong Chui had been deeply troubled because Bao had not yet named an heir of the main line.

sentences.zh: 寶庶子清河公會多材藝，有雄略，垂深奇之。

translations.literal: Bao's son by a concubine, Duke of Qinghe Hui, was gifted in many arts and possessed bold strategy; Chui greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's son by a concubine, the Duke of Qinghe Murong Hui, was accomplished in many fields and possessed bold strategic vision; Chui regarded him with exceptional admiration.

sentences.zh: 及寶之北伐，使會代攝宮事，總錄、禮遇一同太子，所以見定旨也。

translations.literal: When Bao marched north to campaign, he had Hui act in his stead in palace affairs; his overall authority and ceremonial treatment were identical to those of the heir apparent — thus his intended designation was made clear.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao led a northern campaign, he had Hui govern the palace in his absence; Hui's authority and ceremonial standing matched those of the heir apparent, making plain that he was the intended successor.

sentences.zh: 垂之伐魏，以龍城舊都，宗廟所在，復使會鎮幽州，委以東北之重，高選僚屬以崇威望。

translations.literal: When Chui attacked Wei, because Longcheng was the old capital where the ancestral temples stood, he again had Hui garrison You Province, entrusting him with the weight of the northeast and selecting high-ranking subordinates to enhance his prestige.
translations.idiomatic: When Chui campaigned against Wei, he again stationed Hui in You Province to guard Longcheng, the old capital and seat of the ancestral shrines, entrusting him with the security of the northeast and appointing eminent officials to bolster his authority.

sentences.zh: 臨死顧命，以會為寶嗣，而寶寵愛少子濮陽公策，意不在會。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he left instructions that Hui should succeed Bao, but Bao doted on his youngest son, Duke of Puyang Ce, and his heart was not with Hui.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Chui named Hui as Bao's successor, but Bao favored his youngest son, the Duke of Puyang Murong Ce, and had no intention of following that wish.

sentences.zh: 寶庶長子長樂公盛自以同生年長，恥會先之，乃盛稱策宜為儲貳，而非毀會焉。

translations.literal: Bao's eldest son by a concubine, Duke of Changle Sheng, considering himself born of the same mother and older in years, was shamed that Hui should precede him; he therefore loudly praised Ce as fit to be heir and slandered Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's eldest son by a concubine, the Duke of Changle Murong Sheng, resented that Hui, though younger, had been placed ahead of him; he loudly advocated making Ce heir and spoke ill of Hui at every turn.

sentences.zh: 寶大悅，乃訪其趙王麟、高陽王隆，麟等咸希旨贊成之。

translations.literal: Bao was greatly pleased and thereupon consulted Prince of Zhao Lin and Prince of Gaoyang Long; Lin and the others all conformed to his intent and endorsed it.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was delighted and consulted the Prince of Zhao Murong Lin and the Prince of Gaoyang Murong Long; Lin and the others all read his wishes and endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 寶遂與麟等定計，立策母段氏為皇后，策為皇太子，盛、會進爵為王。

translations.literal: Bao thereupon settled the plan with Lin and the others: he installed Ce's mother, the Duan clan, as empress, made Ce crown prince, and advanced Sheng and Hui in rank to princes.
translations.idiomatic: Bao then settled the matter with Lin and the others: he made Ce's mother, Lady Duan, empress, named Ce crown prince, and raised Sheng and Hui to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 策字道符，年十一，美姿貌，而蠢弱不慧。

translations.literal: Ce, courtesy name Daofu, was eleven years old, handsome in appearance, yet dull-witted and lacking in intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Ce, whose courtesy name was Daofu, was eleven years old and handsome in bearing, but slow-witted and without discernment.

sentences.zh: 魏伐并州，驃騎農逆戰，敗績，還于晉陽，司馬慕輿嵩閉門距之。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Bing Province, the Cavalry General Nong met them in battle, was defeated, and returned to Jinyang; the Major Murong Song shut the gates and barred him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei invaded Bing Province, the Cavalry General Murong Nong met them in battle, suffered defeat, and withdrew to Jinyang, where the Major Murong Song shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 農率騎數千奔歸中山，行及潞川，為魏追軍所及，餘騎盡沒，單馬遁還。

translations.literal: Nong led several thousand horsemen in flight back to Zhongshan; when he reached the Lu River he was overtaken by Wei pursuers, his remaining horsemen were all destroyed, and he escaped alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Nong fled with several thousand horsemen toward Zhongshan; at the Lu River he was overtaken by Wei pursuers, his remaining cavalry were wiped out, and he escaped alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 寶引群臣於東堂議之。

translations.literal: Bao summoned the ministers to the Eastern Hall to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Bao gathered his ministers in the Eastern Hall to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 中山尹苻謨曰：「魏軍強盛，千里轉鬥，乘勝而來，勇氣兼倍，若逸騎平原，形勢彌盛，殆難為敵，宜度險距之。

translations.literal: The Governor of Zhongshan, Fu Mo, said: "The Wei army is powerful; fighting at a distance of a thousand li, they come riding victory, their courage doubled. If we let their cavalry roam the plain, their momentum will grow still greater and they will be hard to oppose. We should cross difficult terrain and block them."
translations.idiomatic: The Governor of Zhongshan, Fu Mo, said: "The Wei forces are formidable. Having fought a thousand li from home, they arrive flushed with victory and doubly bold. If we let their cavalry loose on open ground their advantage will only grow, and they will be nearly impossible to defeat. We should take up a defensible position in difficult country and hold them there."

sentences.zh: 」中書令晆邃曰：「魏軍多騎，師行剽銳，馬上齎糧，不過旬日。

translations.literal: " The Director of the Secretariat, Fei Sui, said: "The Wei army has many horsemen; their columns march with swift ferocity, carrying grain on horseback — they cannot last more than ten days."
translations.idiomatic: " The Director of the Secretariat, Fei Sui, said: "The Wei army is mostly cavalry; their columns move with swift ferocity and carry provisions on horseback — they cannot sustain themselves for more than ten days."

sentences.zh: 宜令郡縣聚千家為一堡，深溝高壘，清野待之。

translations.literal: We should order the commanderies and counties to gather a thousand households into one fort, dig deep ditches and raise high ramparts, and clear the countryside to await them.
translations.idiomatic: We should order the commanderies and counties to gather a thousand households into each fortified settlement, dig deep ditches and raise high ramparts, and clear the countryside to await them.

sentences.zh: 至無所掠，資食無出，不過六旬，自然窮退。

translations.literal: When there is nothing left to plunder and no supplies to draw on, in no more than sixty days they will naturally withdraw in exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Once there is nothing left to plunder and no supplies to be had, within sixty days they will withdraw of their own accord, exhausted.

sentences.zh: 」尚書封懿曰：「今魏師十萬，天下之勍敵也。

translations.literal: " The Master of Writing Feng Yi said: "The Wei host now numbers a hundred thousand — the fiercest enemy under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: " The Master of Writing Feng Yi said: "The Wei host now numbers a hundred thousand men — the fiercest foe in the realm."

sentences.zh: 百姓雖欲營聚，不足自固，是則聚糧集兵以資強寇，且動眾心，示之以弱，阻關距戰，計之上也。

translations.literal: Though the common people may wish to gather in fortified settlements, they are not strong enough to defend themselves; to do so would only amass grain and troops to supply a powerful enemy, stir the hearts of the masses, and show weakness. Blocking the passes and fighting at the frontier is the superior plan."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the people wish to gather in fortified settlements, they cannot hold them; doing so would only stockpile grain and troops for a powerful enemy, unsettle the populace, and advertise weakness. Blocking the passes and meeting them in battle at the frontier is the better plan."

sentences.zh: 」慕容麟曰：「魏今乘勝氣銳，其鋒不可當，宜自完守設備，待其弊而乘之。

translations.literal: " Murong Lin said: "Wei now rides victory with sharp morale; their edge cannot be met. We should complete our defenses and wait until they weaken, then strike."
translations.idiomatic: " Murong Lin said: "Wei now rides the momentum of victory with keen morale; their edge cannot be met head-on. We should fortify our defenses and wait until they weaken, then strike."

sentences.zh: 」於是修城積粟，為持久之備。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they repaired the walls and stockpiled grain, making preparations for a prolonged defense.
translations.idiomatic: " They then repaired the walls, stockpiled grain, and made ready for a prolonged defense.

sentences.zh: 魏攻中山不克，進據博陵魯口，諸將望風奔退，郡縣悉降于魏，寶聞魏有內難，乃盡眾出距，步卒十二萬，騎三萬七千，次於曲陽柏肆。

translations.literal: Wei attacked Zhongshan without success, advanced and occupied Boling Lukou; the generals fled at the mere sight of them, and the commanderies and counties all surrendered to Wei. When Bao heard that Wei had internal troubles, he led out his entire force to resist: a hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers and thirty-seven thousand horsemen, encamped at Qufu and Bosi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei besieged Zhongshan without success, then advanced to occupy Boling Lukou; commanders fled at the mere rumor of their approach, and commanderies and counties surrendered to Wei in succession. Hearing that Wei faced internal troubles, Bao marched out with his full strength to resist: a hundred and twenty thousand infantry and thirty-seven thousand cavalry, encamped at Qufu and Bosi.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進至新梁。

translations.literal: The Wei army advanced to Xinliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army advanced to Xinliang.

sentences.zh: 寶憚魏師之銳，乃遣征北隆夜襲魏軍，敗績而還。

translations.literal: Bao feared the sharpness of the Wei host and sent the Northern Expeditionary Long to raid the Wei camp by night; he was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Wei army's edge, Bao sent the Northern Expeditionary Murong Long to raid the Wei camp by night; Long was defeated and driven back.

sentences.zh: 魏軍方軌而至，對營相持，上下兇懼，三軍奪氣。

translations.literal: The Wei army came on in close order; the two camps faced each other. Above and below were filled with dread, and the three armies lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army advanced in tight formation; the two camps faced each other. Dread spread through every rank, and the army's fighting spirit collapsed.

sentences.zh: 農、麟勸寶還中山，乃引歸。

translations.literal: Nong and Lin urged Bao to return to Zhongshan, and he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Nong and Lin urged Bao to withdraw to Zhongshan, and he turned the army homeward.

sentences.zh: 魏軍追擊之，寶、農等棄大軍，率騎二萬奔還。

translations.literal: The Wei army pursued; Bao, Nong, and the others abandoned the main force and fled back with twenty thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army gave chase; Bao, Nong, and the others abandoned the main body and fled homeward with twenty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 時大風雪，凍死者相枕於道。

translations.literal: At that time a great wind and snow blew; the dead from freezing lay piled along the road.
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard struck; the frozen dead lay heaped along the road.

sentences.zh: 寶恐為魏軍所及，命去袍杖戎器，寸刃無返。

translations.literal: Bao feared the Wei army would overtake him and ordered robes, staffs, and weapons cast aside — not a blade was to be brought back.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing capture by the Wei pursuers, Bao ordered robes, staffs, and weapons thrown away — not a blade was to be carried back.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進攻中山，屯于芳林園。

translations.literal: The Wei army advanced to attack Zhongshan and encamped at Fanglin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army advanced against Zhongshan and encamped at Fanglin Garden.

sentences.zh: 其夜尚書慕容皓謀殺寶，立慕容麟。

translations.literal: That night the Master of Writing Murong Hao plotted to kill Bao and install Murong Lin.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Master of Writing Murong Hao plotted to kill Bao and install Murong Lin on the throne.

sentences.zh: 皓妻兄蘇泥告之，寶使慕容隆收皓，皓與同謀數十人斬關奔魏。

translations.literal: Hao's wife's elder brother Su Ni informed on them; Bao sent Murong Long to arrest Hao; Hao and several dozen co-conspirators cut through the gate and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's brother-in-law Su Ni exposed the plot; Bao sent Murong Long to arrest Hao, but Hao and several dozen conspirators cut through the gate and fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 麟懼不自安，以兵劫左衛將軍、北地王精，謀率禁旅弑寶。

translations.literal: Lin, fearing for his own safety, took troops and seized the Left Guard General, Prince of Beidi Jing, intending to lead the palace guard in assassinating Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, fearing for his own safety, seized the Left Guard General, Prince of Beidi Murong Jing, and plotted to lead the palace guard in assassinating Bao.

sentences.zh: 精以義距之，麟怒，殺精，出奔丁零。

translations.literal: Jing resisted on grounds of righteousness; Lin in anger killed Jing and fled to the Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Jing resisted on grounds of loyalty; Lin in fury killed him and fled to the Dingling.

sentences.zh: 初，寶聞魏之來伐也，使慕容會率幽、并之眾赴中山，麟既叛，寶恐其逆奪會軍，將遣兵迎之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bao heard that Wei was coming to attack, he had sent Murong Hui to lead the forces of You and Bing to hurry to Zhongshan. After Lin rebelled, Bao feared Hui would seize the army in revolt and was about to send troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao first learned of Wei's invasion, he had ordered Murong Hui to lead the armies of You and Bing to Zhongshan. After Lin's rebellion, Bao feared Hui might seize those troops in revolt and prepared to send forces to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 麟侍郎段平子自丁零奔還，說麟招集丁零，軍眾甚盛，謀襲會軍，東據龍城。

translations.literal: Lin's attendant Duan Pingzi fled back from the Dingling and reported that Lin was gathering the Dingling; his host was very large, and he planned to strike Hui's army and seize Longcheng in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's attendant Duan Pingzi fled back from the Dingling and reported that Lin was rallying Dingling forces in great numbers, intending to strike Hui's army and seize Longcheng in the east.

sentences.zh: 寶與其太子策及農、隆等萬餘騎迎會於薊，以開封公慕容詳守中山。

translations.literal: Bao, with his crown prince Ce and Nong, Long, and others — more than ten thousand horsemen — went to meet Hui at Ji; he left the Duke of Kaifeng Murong Xiang to hold Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rode out with more than ten thousand horsemen — the crown prince Ce, Nong, Long, and others — to meet Hui at Ji, leaving the Duke of Kaifeng Murong Xiang to defend Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會傾身誘納，繕甲厲兵，步騎二萬，列陣而進，迎寶薊南。

translations.literal: Hui devoted himself to winning men over, repaired armor and sharpened weapons, and with twenty thousand foot and horse advanced in battle array to meet Bao south of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Hui worked tirelessly to win loyalty, repaired armor and sharpened weapons, and marched south of Ji with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry in battle order to receive Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶分其兵給農，隆，遣西河公庫辱官驥率眾三千助守中山。

translations.literal: Bao divided his troops between Nong and Long and sent the Duke of Xihe Kurou Guan Ji with three thousand men to help hold Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao divided his forces between Nong and Long and sent the Duke of Xihe Kurou Guan Ji with three thousand men to reinforce the defense of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會以策為太子，有恨色。

translations.literal: When Hui saw that Ce had been made crown prince, he showed resentment on his face.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui learned that Ce had been made crown prince, resentment showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 寶以告農、隆，俱曰：「會一年少，專任方事，習驕所致，豈有他也。

translations.literal: Bao told Nong and Long of it; both said: "Hui is still young and has sole charge of frontier affairs; this comes of habitual arrogance — there is surely no other cause.
translations.idiomatic: Bao told Nong and Long; both said: "Hui is still young and holds sole command on the frontier; this is merely the arrogance of office — there is surely nothing more to it.

sentences.zh: 臣當以禮責之。

translations.literal: Your subjects will reprove him by ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: We shall take him to task in the proper ceremonial manner."

sentences.zh: 」幽平之士皆懷會威德，不樂去之，咸請曰：「清河王天資神武，權略過人，臣等與之誓同生死，感王恩澤，皆勇氣自倍。

translations.literal: " The gentlemen of You and Ping all cherished Hui's authority and virtue and were unwilling to leave him; they all petitioned: "The Prince of Qinghe is gifted by Heaven with divine martial prowess and surpasses others in strategy; we have sworn with him to live and die together, and moved by the king's gracious favor our courage is redoubled."
translations.idiomatic: " The officers of You and Ping all revered Hui's authority and virtue and were loath to part from him; they petitioned as one: "The Prince of Qinghe possesses Heaven-given martial genius and strategic gifts beyond ordinary men; we have sworn to live and die with him, and stirred by Your Majesty's gracious favor our courage is redoubled."

sentences.zh: 願陛下與皇太子、諸王止駕薊宮，使王統臣等進解京師之圍，然後奉迎車駕。

translations.literal: We beg Your Majesty, together with the crown prince and the princes, to halt at the Ji palace; let the prince command us to advance and relieve the siege of the capital, and afterward we shall escort the imperial carriage back."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty, together with the crown prince and the princes, to remain at the Ji palace while the prince leads us to raise the siege of the capital; afterward we shall escort the imperial carriage home."

sentences.zh: 」寶左右皆害其勇略，譖而不許，眾咸有怨言。

translations.literal: " Bao's attendants all feared Hui's courage and strategy; they slandered him and the request was denied — resentment spread widely among the troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao's attendants feared Hui's courage and strategic gifts; they slandered him until the request was denied, and discontent spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 左右勸寶殺會，侍御史仇尼歸聞而告會曰：「左右密謀如是，主上將從之。

translations.literal: His attendants urged Bao to kill Hui; the Attending Censor Chou Nigui heard of it and told Hui: "The attendants are secretly plotting thus; the sovereign is about to assent."
translations.idiomatic: Bao's attendants urged him to kill Hui; the Attending Censor Chou Nigui heard of it and warned Hui: "The attendants are secretly plotting along these lines, and the sovereign is about to agree."

sentences.zh: 大王所恃唯父母也，父已異圖；

translations.literal: What the great king relies on is only his parents; the father already harbors other designs;
translations.idiomatic: What you rely on, great prince, is only your parents — and your father already harbors other designs;

sentences.zh: 所杖者兵也，兵已去手，進退路窮，恐無自全之理。

translations.literal: what he leans on is troops, and the troops have already slipped from his hand; advance and retreat alike are cut off, and I fear there is no way to preserve yourself.
translations.idiomatic: what you lean on is your army, and that army has already slipped from your grasp. With advance and retreat alike cut off, I fear there is no path to safety.

sentences.zh: 盍誅二王，廢太子，大王自處東宮，兼領將相，以匡社稷。

translations.literal: Why not kill the two princes, depose the crown prince, and let the great king take the Eastern Palace for yourself while also holding the posts of general and minister, thereby setting the state aright?
translations.idiomatic: Why not kill the two princes, depose the crown prince, and install yourself in the Eastern Palace while also taking command as general and minister — thereby setting the state aright?"

sentences.zh: 」會不從。

translations.literal: Hui did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Hui refused.

sentences.zh: 寶謂農、隆曰：「觀會為變，事當必然，宜早殺之。

translations.literal: Bao said to Nong and Long: "Judging Hui's conduct, rebellion is certain; he should be killed early."
translations.idiomatic: Bao told Nong and Long: "Judging by Hui's conduct, rebellion is inevitable; he should be killed at once."

sentences.zh: 不爾，恐成大禍。

translations.literal: Otherwise I fear a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear a catastrophe."

sentences.zh: 」農曰：「寇賊內侮，中州紛亂，會鎮撫舊都，安眾寧境，及京師有難，萬里星赴，威名之重，可以振服戎狄。

translations.literal: " Nong said: "Bandits and enemies invade within; the central provinces are in turmoil. Hui pacifies the old capital and settles the people and secures the borders; when the capital is in peril he comes from ten thousand li like a star — the weight of his renown can awe and subdue the barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: " Nong said: "Enemies press us from within while the heartland is in turmoil. Hui pacifies the old capital, settles the people, and secures the borders; when the capital faces peril he hurries from afar like a shooting star — the weight of his renown alone can awe the northern tribes into submission."

sentences.zh: 又逆跡未彰，宜且隱忍。

translations.literal: Moreover his rebellious intent is not yet manifest; for the time being we should endure in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his treason is not yet open; for now we should endure in silence."

sentences.zh: 今社稷之危若綴旒然，復內相誅戮，有損威望。

translations.literal: The peril to the altars of state now hangs by a thread; to slaughter one another within would damage our prestige.
translations.idiomatic: The peril to the altars of state now hangs by a thread; to turn on one another within would only sap our authority."

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「會逆心已成，而王等仁慈，不欲去之，恐一旦釁發，必先害諸父，然後及吾。

translations.literal: Bao said: "Hui's rebellious heart is already formed, yet you, my princes, are benevolent and unwilling to remove him; I fear that once trouble breaks out he will first harm the princes, my uncles, and afterward reach me."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "Hui's rebellious intent is already fixed, yet you are too merciful to remove him. I fear that once trouble breaks out he will strike my uncles first and come for me afterward."

sentences.zh: 事敗之後，當思朕言。

translations.literal: After disaster strikes, you will think of my words.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster comes, you will remember what I said today."

sentences.zh: 」農等固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: " Nong and the others pressed their remonstrance, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Nong and the others pressed their remonstrance until he relented.

sentences.zh: 會聞之彌懼，奔于廣都黃榆穀。

translations.literal: When Hui heard of it he grew still more fearful and fled to Huangyu Valley in Guangdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui learned of this he grew still more fearful and fled to Huangyu Valley in Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 會遣仇尼歸等率壯士二千餘人分襲農、隆，隆是夜見殺，農中重創。

translations.literal: Hui sent Chou Nigui and others with more than two thousand stalwarts to attack Nong and Long in separate strikes; Long was killed that night and Nong suffered grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent Chou Nigui and others with more than two thousand stalwarts to strike Nong and Long in separate attacks; Long was killed that night and Nong was gravely wounded.

sentences.zh: 既而會歸於寶，寶意在誅會，誘而安之，潛使左衛慕輿騰斬會，不能傷。

translations.literal: Presently Hui returned to Bao; Bao intended to execute Hui, lured him with reassurances, and secretly sent the Left Guard Murong Teng to cut him down — but could not wound him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then returned to Bao. Bao meant to kill him, lulled him with reassurances, and secretly ordered the Left Guard Murong Teng to strike him down — but failed to wound him.

sentences.zh: 會復奔其眾，於是勒兵攻寶。

translations.literal: Hui again fled to his troops; thereupon he marshaled his forces to attack Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fled again to his troops and thereupon marshaled his forces to attack Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶率數百騎馳如龍城，會率眾追之，遣使請誅左右佞臣，並求太子，寶弗許。

translations.literal: Bao led several hundred horsemen in flight to Longcheng; Hui led his host in pursuit and sent envoys requesting the execution of the sycophantic attendants and also demanding the crown prince; Bao refused.
translations.idiomatic: Bao fled to Longcheng with several hundred horsemen; Hui pursued with his host and sent envoys demanding the execution of the sycophantic attendants and the surrender of the crown prince — Bao refused both.

sentences.zh: 會圍龍城，侍御郎高雲夜率敢死士百餘人襲會，敗之，眾悉逃散，單馬奔還中山，乃逾圍而入，為慕容詳所殺。

translations.literal: Hui besieged Longcheng; the Attendant Gentleman Gao Yun by night led more than a hundred dare-to-die men in a strike against Hui, defeated him, and his host all scattered in flight; he alone on horseback fled back to Zhongshan, crossed the siege lines to enter, and was killed by Murong Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui besieged Longcheng; the Attendant Gentleman Gao Yun led more than a hundred dare-to-die men in a night attack, routed him, and his army scattered; Hui alone fled on horseback to Zhongshan, slipped through the siege lines, and was killed by Murong Xiang.

sentences.zh: 詳僭稱尊號，置百官，改年號。

translations.literal: Xiang presumptuously assumed the title of sovereign, established the hundred offices, and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang presumptuously took the imperial title, established the full bureaucracy, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 荒酒奢淫，殺戮無度，誅其王公以下五百餘人，內外震局，莫敢忤視。

translations.literal: He was dissolute in wine and extravagant in lust, killing without measure; he executed more than five hundred princes and officials down to the common ranks, and within and without trembled — none dared look him in the face.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned himself in wine and debauchery, killing without restraint; he executed more than five hundred princes and officials down to the common ranks, and the court and realm alike trembled — none dared meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 城中大饑，公卿餓死者數十人。

translations.literal: Famine gripped the city; several dozen of the nobility and high officials died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the city; dozens of nobles and high officials starved to death.

sentences.zh: 麟率丁零之眾入中山，斬詳及其親党三百餘人，復僭稱尊號。

translations.literal: Lin led the Dingling host into Zhongshan, executed Xiang and more than three hundred of his kin and partisans, and again presumptuously assumed the title of sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Lin led the Dingling into Zhongshan, executed Xiang and more than three hundred of his kin and partisans, and again presumptuously took the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 中山饑甚，麟出據新市，與魏師戰於義台，麟軍敗績。

translations.literal: Famine in Zhongshan was extreme; Lin went out to occupy Xinshi and fought the Wei host at Yitai; Lin's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Famine in Zhongshan was extreme; Lin marched out to occupy Xinshi and fought the Wei army at Yitai, where his forces were routed.

sentences.zh: 魏師遂人中山，麟乃奔鄴。

translations.literal: The Wei host thereupon entered Zhongshan; Lin fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army then entered Zhongshan; Lin fled to Ye.

sentences.zh: 慕容德遣侍郎李延勸寶南伐，寶大悅，慕容盛切諫，以為兵疲師老，魏新平中原，宜養兵觀釁，更俟他年。

translations.literal: Murong De sent the Attendant Gentleman Li Yan to urge Bao to march south; Bao was greatly pleased. Murong Sheng remonstrated earnestly, holding that the troops were weary and the commanders aged, that Wei had newly pacified the central plain, and that they should nurture their forces, watch for openings, and wait for another year.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De sent the Attendant Gentleman Li Yan to urge Bao to march south; Bao was delighted. Murong Sheng remonstrated earnestly, arguing that the army was exhausted, Wei had newly pacified the central plain, and they should rest their forces, watch for an opening, and wait for another year.

sentences.zh: 寶將從之。

translations.literal: Bao was about to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was about to heed him.

sentences.zh: 撫軍慕輿騰進曰：「今眾旅已集，宜乘新定之機以成進取之功。

translations.literal: The Adjutant Murong Teng advanced and said: "The host is already assembled; we should seize this newly settled moment to accomplish the merit of advance."
translations.idiomatic: The Adjutant Murong Teng stepped forward and said: "The army is already assembled; we should seize this moment of fresh consolidation to win the merit of advance."

sentences.zh: 人可使由之，而難與圖始，惟當獨決聖慮，不足廣采異同，以沮亂軍議也。

translations.literal: Men may be led — it is hard to plan the beginning with them; Your Majesty should decide the sacred intent alone and not widely gather divergent views, lest the army's deliberations be thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Men may be led along afterward, but it is hard to take them into counsel at the outset; Your Majesty should decide alone and not gather too many dissenting views, lest the army's deliberations be thrown into confusion."

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「吾計決矣，敢諫者斬！

translations.literal: Bao said: "My plan is settled; whoever dares remonstrate will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: "My mind is made up; whoever dares remonstrate will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 」寶發龍城，以慕輿騰為前軍大司馬，慕容農為中軍，寶為後軍，步騎三萬，次於乙連。

translations.literal: Bao set out from Longcheng with Murong Teng as Grand Marshal of the vanguard, Murong Nong in the center, and himself in the rear — thirty thousand foot and horse — encamped at Yilian.
translations.idiomatic: Bao marched from Longcheng with Murong Teng as Grand Marshal of the vanguard, Murong Nong commanding the center, and himself in the rear — thirty thousand infantry and cavalry — encamped at Yilian.

sentences.zh: 長上段速骨、宋赤眉因眾軍之憚役也，殺司空、樂浪王宙，逼立高陽王崇。

translations.literal: The senior officer Duan Sugu and Song Chimei, because the troops feared forced labor, killed the Minister of Works, Prince of Lelang Zhou, and compelled the Prince of Gaoyang Chong to be installed.
translations.idiomatic: The senior officer Duan Sugu and Song Chimei, exploiting the troops' fear of forced labor, killed the Minister of Works, Prince of Lelang Murong Zhou, and compelled the Prince of Gaoyang Murong Chong to accept the throne.

sentences.zh: 寶單騎奔農，仍引軍討速骨。

translations.literal: Bao fled alone on horseback to Nong and then led troops to punish Sugu.
translations.idiomatic: Bao fled alone to Nong and then led troops against Sugu.

sentences.zh: 眾咸憚征幸亂，投杖奔之。

translations.literal: The host all feared the campaign and the turmoil; they cast aside their weapons and fled to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The troops feared both the campaign and the turmoil; they threw down their weapons and fled to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 騰眾亦潰，寶、農馳還龍城。

translations.literal: Teng's host also collapsed; Bao and Nong galloped back to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Teng's force also collapsed; Bao and Nong galloped back to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗潛與速骨通謀，速骨進師攻城，農為蘭汗所譎，潛出赴賊，為速骨所殺。

translations.literal: Lan Han secretly conspired with Sugu; Sugu advanced to besiege the city. Nong was deceived by Lan Han, slipped out secretly to join the rebels, and was killed by Sugu.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han secretly conspired with Sugu; Sugu advanced to besiege the city. Nong was deceived by Lan Han, slipped out secretly to join the rebels, and was killed by Sugu.

sentences.zh: 眾皆奔散，寶與慕容盛、慕輿騰等南奔。

translations.literal: The host all scattered in flight; Bao fled south with Murong Sheng, Murong Teng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The army scattered; Bao fled south with Murong Sheng, Murong Teng, and others.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗奉太子策承制，遣使迎寶，及於薊城。

translations.literal: Lan Han, acting in the crown prince's name, sent envoys to welcome Bao; they met at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han, acting in the crown prince's name, sent envoys to welcome Bao; they met him at Ji.

sentences.zh: 寶欲還北，盛等咸以汗之忠款虛實未明，今單馬而還，汗有貳志者，悔之無及。

translations.literal: Bao wished to return north; Sheng and the others all held that Han's loyalty was not yet clear in truth or falsehood — if he returned alone on horseback and Han harbored other intent, there would be no recalling the mistake.
translations.idiomatic: Bao wished to return north; Sheng and the others argued that Han's loyalty was still unproved — if Bao rode back alone and Han harbored treachery, the mistake could not be undone.

sentences.zh: 寶從之，乃自薊而南。

translations.literal: Bao followed this and turned south from Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Bao took their counsel and turned south from Ji.

sentences.zh: 至黎陽，聞慕容德稱制，懼而退。

translations.literal: When he reached Liyang he heard that Murong De had assumed power and, fearing, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang he learned that Murong De had assumed independent authority and, alarmed, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遣慕輿騰招集散兵于钜鹿，慕容盛結豪桀于冀州，段儀、段溫收部曲于內黃，眾皆響會，克期將集。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Teng to gather scattered troops at Julu; Murong Sheng rallied bold men in Ji Province; Duan Yi and Duan Wen gathered their followings at Neihuang — all answered the summons, fixing a date to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Murong Teng to rally scattered troops at Julu; Murong Sheng gathered bold men in Ji Province; Duan Yi and Duan Wen mustered their followings at Neihuang — all answered the call and fixed a date to assemble.

sentences.zh: 會蘭汗遣左將軍蘇超迎寶，寶以汗垂之季舅，盛又汗之壻也，必謂忠款無貳，乃還至龍城。

translations.literal: Then Lan Han sent the Left General Su Chao to welcome Bao; Bao, because Han was Chui's youngest maternal uncle and Sheng was also Han's son-in-law, believed his loyalty could not be divided and returned to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Then Lan Han sent the Left General Su Chao to welcome Bao; Bao, considering Han Chui's youngest maternal uncle and Sheng Han's son-in-law, judged his loyalty secure and returned to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 汗引寶入于外邸，弑之，時年四十四，在位三年，即隆安三年也。

translations.literal: Han led Bao into the outer residence and assassinated him; he was forty-four years old and had reigned three years — the third year of Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: Han led Bao into the outer residence and assassinated him; he was forty-four and had reigned three years — the third year of the Long'an era.

sentences.zh: 汗又殺其太子策及王公卿士百餘人。

translations.literal: Han also killed the crown prince Ce and more than a hundred princes, dukes, and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Han also killed the crown prince Ce and more than a hundred princes, dukes, and ministers.

sentences.zh: 汗自稱大都督、大將軍、大單于、昌黎王。

translations.literal: Han himself styled himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Han styled himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Changli.

sentences.zh: 盛僭位，偽諡寶惠湣皇帝，廟號烈宗。

translations.literal: Sheng presumptuously took the throne and gave Bao the posthumous title Emperor Hui Min, with temple name Lie Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng took the throne and posthumously titled Bao Emperor Hui Min, with the temple name Lie Zong.

sentences.zh: 皝之遷于龍城也，植松為社主。

translations.literal: When Huang moved the capital to Longcheng, he planted pines as the lord of the soil altar.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Huang moved the capital to Longcheng, he planted pines to serve as the spirit of the soil altar.

sentences.zh: 及秦滅燕，大風吹拔之。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Yan, a great wind blew and uprooted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin destroyed Yan, a great wind uprooted them.

sentences.zh: 後數年，社處忽有桑二根生焉。

translations.literal: Several years later, at the site of the altar two mulberry roots suddenly sprang up.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, two mulberry roots suddenly sprang up at the altar site.

sentences.zh: 先是，遼川無桑，及廆通于晉，求種江南，平州桑悉由吳來。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liaochuan had no mulberry; when Hui opened relations with Jin he sought seed from south of the Yangtze, and the mulberry of Ping Province all came from Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Liaochuan had no mulberry trees; when Murong Hui opened relations with Jin he sought seedlings from south of the Yangtze, and all the mulberry of Ping Province came from Wu.

sentences.zh: 廆終而垂以吳王中興，寶之將敗，大風又拔其一。

translations.literal: When Hui died, Chui revived Wu as king; when Bao was about to fall, the great wind again uprooted one of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Hui died, Murong Chui revived the fortunes of Wu; when Bao was about to fall, the great wind uprooted one of the mulberries again.

sentences.zh: 盛字道運，寶之庶長子也。

translations.literal: Sheng, courtesy name Daoyun, was Bao's eldest son by a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, whose courtesy name was Daoyun, was Bao's eldest son by a concubine.

sentences.zh: 少沈敏，多謀略。

translations.literal: In youth he was deep and keen, with many stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was reserved and sharp, possessed of many stratagems.

sentences.zh: 苻堅誅慕容氏，盛潛奔於沖。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian executed the Murong clan, Sheng secretly fled to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian executed the Murong clan, Sheng secretly fled to Murong Chong.

sentences.zh: 及沖稱尊號，有自得之志，賞罰不均，政令不明。

translations.literal: When Chong assumed the imperial title he had a mind full of self-satisfaction; rewards and punishments were uneven and government orders unclear.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong took the imperial title he grew complacent; rewards and punishments were uneven and his orders unclear.

sentences.zh: 盛年十二，謂叔父柔曰：「今中山王智不先眾，才不出下，恩未施人，先自驕大，以盛觀之，鮮不覆敗。

translations.literal: Sheng at twelve said to his uncle Rou: "The Prince of Zhongshan now — his wisdom does not lead the multitude, his talent does not surpass his inferiors, his favor has not been shown to men, yet he is already proud and grand; as I see it, he will scarcely escape ruin."
translations.idiomatic: At twelve Sheng told his uncle Rou: "The Prince of Zhongshan is neither wiser than the crowd nor more talented than his subordinates, yet he has shown no kindness to others and already thinks himself grand — in my view he will hardly escape ruin."

sentences.zh: 」俄而沖為段木延所殺，盛隨慕容永東如長子，謂柔曰：「今崎嶇於鋒刃之間，在疑忌之際，愚則為人所猜，智則危甚巢幕，當如鴻鵠高飛，一舉萬里，不可坐待罟網也。

translations.literal: " Presently Chong was killed by Duan Muyan; Sheng followed Murong Yong east to Changzi and said to Rou: "We now tread a rugged path between blades; we stand in a moment of suspicion — if foolish we will be suspected by others, if wise we are as perilous as birds in a nest before a curtain. We should soar like wild swans ten thousand li in a single flight and not sit waiting for the net."
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Chong was killed by Duan Muyan; Sheng followed Murong Yong east to Changzi and told Rou: "We now walk a knife-edge amid suspicion — play the fool and men will suspect us, play the wise and we are birds in a burning nest. We must rise like wild swans and fly ten thousand li at a stroke, not sit waiting for the net."

sentences.zh: 」於是與柔及弟會間行東歸於慕容垂。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he traveled secretly east with Rou and his younger brother Hui to join Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: " He then traveled secretly east with Rou and his younger brother Hui to join Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 遇盜陝中，盛曰：「我六尺之軀，入水不溺，在火不焦，汝欲當吾鋒乎！

translations.literal: They met bandits in the Shaan gorge; Sheng said: "My six-chi frame — enter water and I do not drown, enter fire and I am not burned; do you wish to meet my edge?"
translations.idiomatic: They met bandits in the Shaan gorge; Sheng said: "This body of mine does not drown in water or burn in fire — do you wish to test my blade?"

sentences.zh: 試豎爾手中箭百步，我若中之，宜慎爾命，如其不中，當束身相授。

translations.literal: Set up your arrow in hand at a hundred paces; if I hit it, guard your life carefully; if I do not, I shall bind myself and surrender to you.
translations.idiomatic: Plant your arrow at a hundred paces; if I hit it, spare your life; if I miss, I will bind myself and surrender.

sentences.zh: 」盜用豎箭，盛一發中之。

translations.literal: " The bandit used his raised arrow; Sheng with one shot hit it.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandit raised his arrow; Sheng struck it with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 盜曰：「郎貴人之子，故相試耳。

translations.literal: The bandit said: "Young master, you are a nobleman's son — I was only testing you."
translations.idiomatic: The bandit said: "Young lord, you are a nobleman's son — I was only testing you."

sentences.zh: 」資而遣之。

translations.literal: " He supplied them and sent them on.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave them provisions and sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，永誅俊、垂之子孫，男女無遺。

translations.literal: After more than a year Yong executed Jun and Chui's descendants, men and women without remnant.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Yong executed Murong Jun and all of Chui's descendants, men and women alike, without exception.

sentences.zh: 盛既至，垂問以西事，畫地成圖。

translations.literal: When Sheng arrived, Chui questioned him on western affairs and he drew a map on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng arrived, Chui questioned him about affairs in the west and he traced a map on the ground.

sentences.zh: 垂笑曰：「昔魏武撫明帝之首，遂乃侯之，祖之愛孫，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Chui smiled and said: "In old times Emperor Wu of Wei stroked Mingdi's head and thereafter enfeoffed him — a grandfather's love for a grandson has its source from of old."
translations.idiomatic: Chui smiled and said: "Long ago Cao Cao stroked Emperor Ming's head and thereafter enfeoffed him — a grandfather's love for a grandson is an old story."

sentences.zh: 」於是封長樂公。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he enfeoffed him as Duke of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon enfeoffed him as Duke of Changle.

sentences.zh: 驍勇剛毅，有伯父全之風烈。

translations.literal: Fierce and brave, firm and resolute, he had the martial splendor of his uncle Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce, resolute, and bold, he bore the martial spirit of his uncle Murong Quan.

sentences.zh: 寶即偽位，進爵為王。

translations.literal: When Bao took the usurped throne, Sheng was advanced in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao took the throne, Sheng was raised to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 寶自龍城南伐，盛留統後事，及段速骨作亂，馳出迎衛。

translations.literal: When Bao marched south from Longcheng, Sheng remained to oversee rear affairs; when Duan Sugu rebelled, he galloped out to meet and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao marched south from Longcheng, Sheng remained to manage affairs at home; when Duan Sugu rebelled, he galloped out to protect him.

sentences.zh: 寶幾為速骨所獲，賴盛以免。

translations.literal: Bao was nearly taken by Sugu; he escaped only through Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was nearly captured by Sugu and escaped only thanks to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 盛屢進奇策於寶，寶不能從，是以屢敗。

translations.literal: Sheng repeatedly offered bold stratagems to Bao, but Bao could not follow them, and therefore suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng repeatedly offered bold stratagems to Bao, but Bao would not heed them and so suffered defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 寶既如龍城，盛留在後。

translations.literal: After Bao reached Longcheng, Sheng remained behind.
translations.idiomatic: After Bao reached Longcheng, Sheng stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 寶為蘭汗所殺，盛馳進赴哀，將軍張真固諫以為不可，盛曰：「我今投命，告以哀窮。

translations.literal: When Bao was killed by Lan Han, Sheng galloped forward to mourn; the general Zhang Zhengu remonstrated that he should not, but Sheng said: "I now cast myself on their mercy and plead our grief and destitution."
translations.idiomatic: When Bao was killed by Lan Han, Sheng hurried forward to mourn; the general Zhang Zhengu urged him not to go, but Sheng said: "I now throw myself on their mercy and plead our grief and destitution."

sentences.zh: 汗性愚近，必顧念婚姻，不忍害我。

translations.literal: Han's nature is foolish and narrow; he will surely think of the marriage bond and be unwilling to harm me.
translations.idiomatic: Han is dull and shortsighted; he will surely remember the marriage tie and be unwilling to harm me.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，足展吾志。

translations.literal: Within a month or so I shall have room enough to carry out my purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month I shall have room enough to carry out my design.

sentences.zh: 」遂人赴喪。

translations.literal: " He thereupon entered to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went in to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 汗妻乙氏泣涕請盛，汗亦哀之，遣其子穆迎盛，舍之宮內，親敬如舊。

translations.literal: Han's wife, the Yi clan, wept and pleaded for Sheng; Han also pitied him, sent his son Mu to welcome Sheng, lodged him within the palace, and treated him with the same intimate respect as before.
translations.idiomatic: Han's wife Lady Yi wept and pleaded for Sheng; Han pitied him too, sent his son Mu to welcome him, lodged him in the palace, and treated him with the same intimate respect as before.

sentences.zh: 汗兄提、弟難勸汗殺盛，汗不從。

translations.literal: Han's elder brother Ti and younger brother Nan urged Han to kill Sheng; Han would not.
translations.idiomatic: Han's elder brother Ti and younger brother Nan urged Han to kill Sheng, but Han refused.

sentences.zh: 慕容奇，汗之外孫也，汗亦宥之。

translations.literal: Murong Qi was Han's grandson by a daughter; Han also spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Qi was Han's grandson by a daughter; Han spared him as well.

sentences.zh: 奇入見盛，遂相與謀。

translations.literal: Qi entered to see Sheng, and they thereupon plotted together.
translations.idiomatic: Qi came to see Sheng, and together they laid their plans.

sentences.zh: 盛遣奇起兵於外，眾至數千。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Qi to raise troops outside; his host reached several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent Qi to raise troops abroad; his force grew to several thousand.

sentences.zh: 汗遣蘭提討奇。

translations.literal: Han sent Lan Ti to punish Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Lan Ti to suppress Qi.

sentences.zh: 提驕很淫荒，事汗無禮，盛因間之於汗曰：「奇，小兒也，未能辦此，必內有應之者。

translations.literal: Ti was arrogant, cruel, and dissolute, serving Han without ritual propriety; Sheng used the opening to say to Han: "Qi is a mere boy and cannot have accomplished this — there must be someone within responding to him."
translations.idiomatic: Ti was arrogant, cruel, and dissolute and served Han without proper respect; Sheng seized the chance to tell Han: "Qi is only a boy and cannot have done this alone — someone within must be backing him."

sentences.zh: 提素驕，不可委以大眾。

translations.literal: Ti has always been arrogant and cannot be entrusted with a great host.
translations.idiomatic: Ti has always been arrogant and cannot be trusted with a large army.

sentences.zh: 」汗因發怒，收提誅之，遣其撫軍仇尼慕率眾討奇。

translations.literal: " Han thereupon grew angry, seized Ti and executed him, and sent his Adjutant Chou Nimu to lead the host against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " Han flew into a rage, arrested Ti and executed him, then sent his Adjutant Chou Nimu with an army against Qi.

sentences.zh: 汗兄弟見提之誅，莫不危懼，皆阻兵背汗，襲敗慕軍。

translations.literal: When Han's brothers saw Ti's execution, none were not filled with dread; they all raised troops in defiance of Han and struck down Mu's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Han's brothers saw Ti executed, all were terrified; each raised troops against Han and routed Mu's army.

sentences.zh: 汗大懼，遣其子穆率眾討之。

translations.literal: Han was greatly afraid and sent his son Mu to lead the host against them.
translations.idiomatic: Han was greatly alarmed and sent his son Mu to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 穆謂汗曰：「慕容盛，我之仇也。

translations.literal: Mu said to Han: "Murong Sheng is my enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Mu told Han: "Murong Sheng is my enemy."

sentences.zh: 奇今起逆，盛必應之。

translations.literal: Qi now rises in rebellion; Sheng is sure to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi now rebels; Sheng is sure to answer him.

sentences.zh: 兼內有蕭牆之難，不宜養心腹之疾。

translations.literal: Moreover there is trouble within the inner quarters — we should not nurture a disease of the vitals.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover trouble stirs within the palace — we must not harbor a disease at the heart.

sentences.zh: 」汗將誅盛，引見察之。

translations.literal: " Han was about to execute Sheng and summoned him to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: " Han was about to kill Sheng and summoned him for a look.

sentences.zh: 盛妻以告，於是偽稱疾篤，不復出入，汗乃止。

translations.literal: Sheng's wife told him; he thereupon feigned grave illness and no longer went in or out, and Han desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's wife warned him; he feigned grave illness and no longer went abroad, and Han desisted.

sentences.zh: 有李旱、衛雙、劉志、張豪、張真者，皆盛之舊昵，蘭穆引為腹心。

translations.literal: There were Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhi, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen — all Sheng's old intimates whom Lan Mu drew into his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhi, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen were all Sheng's old intimates whom Lan Mu drew into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 旱等屢入見盛，潛結大謀。

translations.literal: Han and the others repeatedly entered to see Sheng and secretly formed a great plot.
translations.idiomatic: They repeatedly visited Sheng and secretly formed a great conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 會穆討蘭難等斬之，大饗將士，汗、穆皆醉。

translations.literal: When Mu went out to punish Lan Nan and the others and beheaded them, he held a great feast for officers; Han and Mu were both drunk.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu marched out to punish Lan Nan and the others and beheaded them, he held a great feast for the officers; Han and Mu both grew drunk.

sentences.zh: 盛夜因如廁，袒而逾牆，入於東宮，與李旱等誅穆，眾皆踴呼，進攻汗，斬之。

translations.literal: Sheng by night went out as if to the privy, bared himself and climbed over the wall, entered the Eastern Palace, and with Li Han and the others killed Mu; the host all leapt and shouted, advanced to attack Han, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng slipped out at night as if to the privy, stripped, climbed the wall, entered the Eastern Palace, and with Li Han and the others killed Mu; the troops shouted and stormed Han's quarters and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 汗二子魯公和、陳公楊分屯令支、白狼，遣李旱、張真襲誅之。

translations.literal: Han's two sons, Duke of Lu He and Duke of Chen Yang, were stationed separately at Lingzhi and Bailang; he sent Li Han and Zhang Zhen in surprise attacks to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Han's two sons, the Duke of Lu He and the Duke of Chen Yang, held Lingzhi and Bailang; Sheng sent Li Han and Zhang Zhen to strike and kill them.

sentences.zh: 於是內外怗然，士女咸悅，盛謙揖自卑，不稱尊號。

translations.literal: Thereupon within and without were settled; gentlemen and ladies alike rejoiced; Sheng with humble yielding lowered himself and did not assume the title of sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the realm grew calm; men and women rejoiced alike; Sheng with humble modesty refused to take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 其年，以長樂王稱制，赦其境內，改元曰建平。

translations.literal: That year, as Prince of Changle he assumed regency, amnestied the realm, and changed the reign title to Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Prince of Changle he assumed regency, declared an amnesty throughout the realm, and changed the reign title to Jianping.

sentences.zh: 諸王降爵為公，文武各復舊位。

translations.literal: The princes were reduced in rank to dukes; civil and military officers all resumed their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were reduced to dukes and civil and military officers resumed their former posts.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容奇聚眾于建安，將討蘭汗，百姓翕然從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Qi had gathered troops at Jian'an intending to punish Lan Han; the common people all flocked to him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Murong Qi had gathered troops at Jian'an to move against Lan Han, and the people flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 汗遣兄子全討奇，奇擊滅之，進屯乙連。

translations.literal: Han sent his elder brother's son Quan to punish Qi; Qi struck and destroyed him, then advanced and encamped at Yilian.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent his nephew Quan against Qi; Qi destroyed him and advanced to encamp at Yilian.

sentences.zh: 盛既誅汗，命奇罷兵，奇遂與丁零嚴生、烏丸王龍之阻兵叛盛，引軍至橫溝，去龍城十里。

translations.literal: After Sheng had executed Han, he ordered Qi to disband his troops; Qi thereupon with the Dingling Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan king Long Zhi raised troops in rebellion against Sheng, led his army to Henggou ten li from Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Sheng killed Han he ordered Qi to disband; Qi instead joined the Dingling leader Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan king Long Zhi in rebellion, advancing to Henggou ten li from Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 盛出兵擊敗之，執奇而還，斬龍、生等百餘人。

translations.literal: Sheng led troops out, defeated them, seized Qi and returned, and beheaded Long, Sheng, and more than a hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng marched out, defeated them, seized Qi, and beheaded Long, Sheng, and more than a hundred others.

sentences.zh: 盛於是僭即尊位，大赦殊死已下，追尊伯考獻莊太子全為獻莊皇帝，尊寶後段氏為皇太后，全妃丁氏為獻莊皇后，諡太子策為獻哀太子。

translations.literal: Sheng thereupon presumptuously assumed the imperial title, proclaimed a general amnesty below the grade of capital offense, posthumously honored his uncle by courtesy the Heir Apparent Xianzhuang Quan as Emperor Xianzhuang, honored Bao's consort the Duan clan as Empress Dowager, Quan's consort the Ding clan as Empress Xianzhuang, and gave the posthumous title Heir Apparent Xian'ai to the crown prince Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then took the imperial title, proclaimed a general amnesty short of capital crimes, posthumously honored his uncle the Heir Apparent Xianzhuang Murong Quan as Emperor Xianzhuang, made Bao's consort Lady Duan Empress Dowager and Quan's consort Lady Ding Empress Xianzhuang, and gave the crown prince Ce the posthumous title Heir Apparent Xian'ai.

sentences.zh: 盛幽州刺史慕容豪、尚書左僕射張通、昌黎尹張順謀叛，盛皆誅之。

translations.literal: Murong Hao, Inspector of You Province, Zhang Tong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Zhang Shun, Governor of Changli, plotted rebellion; Sheng executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hao, Inspector of You Province, Zhang Tong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Zhang Shun, Governor of Changli, plotted rebellion; Sheng executed them all.

sentences.zh: 改年為長樂。

translations.literal: He changed the reign title to Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the reign title to Changle.

sentences.zh: 有犯罪者，十日一自決之，無撾捶之罰，而獄情多實。

translations.literal: Criminals were judged by self-confession once every ten days; there was no beating punishment, yet the truth of cases was mostly established.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals confessed once every ten days; there was no flogging, yet cases were mostly judged on truth.

sentences.zh: 高句驪王安遣使貢方物，有雀素身綠首，集於端門，棲翔東園，二旬而去，改東園為白雀園。

translations.literal: The king of Koguryŏ sent envoys with regional tribute; a sparrow of plain white body and green head alighted at the Gate of Correct Deportment, roosted and flew in the Eastern Garden for twenty days and departed; the Eastern Garden was renamed White Sparrow Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Koguryŏ sent tribute; a sparrow with a white body and green head alighted at the main gate, dwelt in the Eastern Garden for twenty days, then departed — and the garden was renamed White Sparrow Garden.

sentences.zh: 盛聽詩歌及周公之事，顧謂群臣曰：「周公之輔成王，不能以至誠感上下，誅兄弟以杜流言，猶擅美于經傳，歌德於管弦。

translations.literal: Sheng listened to songs and the affairs of the Duke of Zhou; he turned to the ministers and said: "The Duke of Zhou's assisting King Cheng — he could not move superiors and inferiors by utmost sincerity, executed his brothers to stop slander, yet still monopolizes beauty in the classics and sings his virtue to pipes and strings."
translations.idiomatic: Listening to songs about the Duke of Zhou, Sheng turned to his ministers and said: "The Duke of Zhou's service to King Cheng — he could not win the hearts of high and low by sincerity alone, killed his brothers to silence rumor, yet still monopolizes praise in the classics and sings his virtue to music."

sentences.zh: 至如我之太宰桓王，承百王之季，主在可奪之年，二寇窺窬，難過往日，臨朝輔政，群情緝穆，經略外敷，辟境千里，以禮讓維宗親，德刑制群後，敦睦雍熙，時無二論。

translations.literal: As for my Grand Preceptor Prince Huan, he inherited the age after a hundred kings, when the sovereign was in years when the throne might be seized; two invaders peered in, their difficulty surpassing former days; he assisted at court and governed the realm, all hearts were harmonized, his external strategy extended a thousand li, he maintained the clan by ritual yielding, governed the host by virtue and punishment, and fostered harmony — for a time there was no second opinion.
translations.idiomatic: But my Grand Preceptor Prince Huan inherited an age after a hundred kings, when the throne stood in years that might be seized; two enemies pressed in with difficulties surpassing any former day; he governed at court, harmonized all hearts, extended the borders a thousand li abroad, bound the clan by ritual yielding and ruled the host by virtue and law, fostering harmony until none dissented.

sentences.zh: 勳道之茂，豈可與周公同日而言乎！

translations.literal: Can the abundance of his merit be spoken of on the same day as the Duke of Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: Can such merit be mentioned in the same breath as the Duke of Zhou's!

sentences.zh: 而燕詠闕而不論，盛德掩而不述，非所謂也。

translations.literal: Yet Yan songs omit him and do not discuss him; great virtue is covered and not recounted — this is not what is called for.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yan songs pass him over in silence and great virtue goes unrecorded — this will not do."

sentences.zh: 」乃命中書更為《燕頌》以述恪之功焉。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered the Masters of Writing to compose anew the "Song of Yan" to recount Ke's achievements.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the Masters of Writing to compose anew the "Song of Yan" to recount Murong Ke's achievements.

sentences.zh: 又引中書令常忠、尚書陽璆、秘書監郎敷於東堂，問曰：「古來君子皆謂周公忠聖，豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: He also summoned the Director of the Secretariat Chang Zhong, the Master of Writing Yang Qiu, and the Director of the Secretariat Bureau Lang Fu to the Eastern Hall and asked: "The gentlemen of old all call the Duke of Zhou loyal and sagely — is this not mistaken!"
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned the Director of the Secretariat Chang Zhong, the Master of Writing Yang Qiu, and the Secretariat Director Lang Fu to the Eastern Hall and asked: "Men of old all call the Duke of Zhou loyal and sagely — are they not mistaken?"

sentences.zh: 」璆曰：「周公居攝政之重，而能達群臣之名，及流言之謗，致烈風以悟主，道契神靈，義光萬代，故累葉稱其高，後王無以奪其美。

translations.literal: " Qiu said: "The Duke of Zhou held the weight of regency yet could make known the names of the ministers; when slander spread he sent a fierce wind to move the sovereign — his Way matched the spirits, his righteousness illumined ten thousand generations; therefore age after age praises his height and later kings cannot displace his beauty."
translations.idiomatic: " Qiu said: "The Duke of Zhou bore the weight of regency yet could win the ministers' names to light; when slander spread he moved Heaven with a fierce wind to awaken the king — his Way matched the spirits and his righteousness lights ten thousand generations; age after age praises his height and later kings cannot displace his glory."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「常令以為何如？

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Director Chang, what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "Director Chang, what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「昔武王疾篤，周公有請令之誠，流言之際，義感天地，楚撻伯禽以訓就王德。

translations.literal: " Zhong said: "In old times King Wu was gravely ill and the Duke of Zhou had the sincerity of praying to yield his life; at the moment of slander his righteousness moved Heaven and Earth; he flogged the Duke of Bo to train and complete the king's virtue."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong said: "When King Wu lay gravely ill, the Duke of Zhou prayed to yield his own life; at the moment of slander his righteousness moved Heaven and Earth; he flogged the Duke of Bo to complete the king's virtue."

sentences.zh: 周公為臣之忠，聖達之美，《詩》《書》已來未之有也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou's loyalty as minister and sagely excellence — since the Odes and Documents there has been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou's loyalty as minister and sagely excellence — since the Odes and Documents there has been nothing like it."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「異哉二君之言！

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Strange are the words of you two gentlemen!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "How strange are your words!"

sentences.zh: 朕見周公之詐，未見其忠聖也。

translations.literal: I see the Duke of Zhou's deceit and have not seen his loyalty and sageliness.
translations.idiomatic: I see the Duke of Zhou's deceit, not his loyalty and sageliness.

sentences.zh: 昔武王得九齡之夢，白文王，文王曰：「我百，爾九十，吾與爾三焉。

translations.literal: In old times King Wu received the dream of the nine-year span and told King Wen; Wen said: "I a hundred, you ninety — I give you three of mine."
translations.idiomatic: Long ago King Wu dreamed the nine-year span and told King Wen; Wen said: "I have a hundred years, you ninety — I give you three of mine."

sentences.zh: 」及文王之終，已驗武王之壽矣。

translations.literal: " When Wen died, King Wu's lifespan had already been verified.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wen died, King Wu's allotted span had already been confirmed.

sentences.zh: 武王之算未盡而求代其死，是非詐乎！

translations.literal: King Wu's tally was not yet exhausted yet he sought to die in his stead — is this not deceit!
translations.idiomatic: King Wu's years were not yet spent yet the Duke sought to die in his place — is this not deceit!

sentences.zh: 若惑於天命，是不聖也。

translations.literal: If he was deluded by Heaven's command, he was not sagely.
translations.idiomatic: If he was deluded by Heaven's mandate, he was not sagely.

sentences.zh: 據攝天位而丹誠不見，致兄弟之間有干戈之事。

translations.literal: He held the regency of Heaven's throne yet his red sincerity was not seen, and between brothers there arose affairs of arms.
translations.idiomatic: He seized regency of the throne yet showed no true loyalty, and between brothers war arose.

sentences.zh: 夫文王之化，自近及遠，故曰刑于寡妻，至於兄弟。

translations.literal: King Wen's transformation proceeded from what was near to what was far — thus it is said: model for the wife, reaching to brothers.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen's teaching spread from near to far — thus it is said: begin with the wife, reach to brothers.

sentences.zh: 周公親違聖父之典而蹈嫌疑之蹤，戮罰同氣以逞私忿，何忠之有乎！

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou personally violated his sage father's canon and trod a path of suspicion, punished those of the same bone to vent private anger — where is the loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: The Duke personally violated his sage father's example and walked a path of suspicion, punished his own kin to vent private wrath — where is the loyalty!

sentences.zh: 但時無直筆之史，後儒承其謬談故也。

translations.literal: But in that age there was no historian with a straight brush; later Confucians inherited their false talk — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: But there was no historian with an upright brush in that age; later Confucians inherited their false tales — that is all."

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「啟金縢而返風，亦足以明其不詐。

translations.literal: " Zhong said: "Opening the golden coffer and the wind's return is also enough to show he was not deceitful."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong said: "Opening the golden coffer and the returning wind is proof enough that he was not deceitful."

sentences.zh: 遭二叔流言之變，而能大義滅親，終安宗國，復子明辟，輔成大業，以致太平，制禮作樂，流慶無窮，亦不可謂非至德也。

translations.literal: He met the slander of the two uncles yet could extinguish kinship in great righteousness, in the end secured the ancestral state, restored the son and clarified the regency, assisted in accomplishing the great enterprise, brought peace, established rites and made music, and his flowing blessing is without end — one also cannot say this was not utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He faced the two uncles' slander yet could sacrifice kin for the greater good, secured the state, restored the son and clarified the regency, assisted the great enterprise, brought peace, established rites and music, and his blessing flows without end — one cannot call this less than utmost virtue."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「卿徒因成文而未原大理，朕今相為論之。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "You only follow finished texts and have not traced the great principle; I shall now debate this with you."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "You only follow finished texts and have not traced the great principle; I shall debate this with you now."

sentences.zh: 昔周自後稷積德累仁，至於文、武。

translations.literal: In old times Zhou from Hou Ji accumulated virtue and benevolence down to Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zhou from Hou Ji onward accumulated virtue and benevolence down to Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 文、武以大聖應期，遂有天下。

translations.literal: Wen and Wu with great sageliness answered the age and thereupon possessed All under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Wu with great sageliness answered the age and took All under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 生靈仰其德，四海歸其仁。

translations.literal: Living creatures looked up to their virtue; the four seas returned to their benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The people looked up to their virtue; the four seas returned to their benevolence.

sentences.zh: 成王雖幼統洪業，而卜世修長，加呂、召、毛、畢為之師傅。

translations.literal: King Cheng though young inherited the great enterprise, yet the generations of his house were long in fortune; moreover Lü, Shao, Mao, and Bi served as his tutors.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng though young inherited the great enterprise, yet the house was long in fortune; Lü, Shao, Mao, and Bi served as his tutors.

sentences.zh: 若無周公攝政，王道足以成也。

translations.literal: If there had been no Duke of Zhou as regent, the kingly Way would have been sufficient to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Without the Duke of Zhou as regent, the kingly Way would have been sufficient to prevail.

sentences.zh: 周公無故以安危為己任，專臨朝之權，闕北面之禮。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou without cause took safety and peril as his own charge, monopolized the authority of facing the court, and neglected the ritual of facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke without cause made the realm's safety his private charge, monopolized court authority, and neglected the ritual of facing north.

sentences.zh: 管、蔡忠存王室，以為周公代主非人臣之道，故言公將不利於孺子。

translations.literal: Guan and Cai loyally preserved the royal house and thought the Duke's replacing the sovereign was not the Way of a minister; therefore they said the Duke would be unfavorable to the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Cai loyally upheld the royal house and held that the Duke's replacing the sovereign was not a minister's Way; therefore they said the Duke would harm the young king.

sentences.zh: 周公當明大順之節，陳誠義以曉群疑，而乃阻兵都邑，擅行誅戮。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou ought to have made clear the great principle of obedience, set forth sincere righteousness to enlighten the host of doubts — yet he instead blocked troops at the capital and arbitrarily carried out executions.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke should have proclaimed the great principle of obedience and set forth sincere righteousness to clear doubts — yet he blocked troops at the capital and executed at will.

sentences.zh: 不臣之罪彰于海內，方貽王《鴟鴞》之詩，歸非於主，是何謂乎！

translations.literal: The crime of disloyalty was manifest within the seas; he was just then presenting to the king the Ode of the Owl, turning blame upon the sovereign — what is this called!
translations.idiomatic: His disloyalty was manifest throughout the realm; he presented the king the Ode of the Owl, turning blame upon his lord — what is this!

sentences.zh: 又周公舉事，稱告二公，二公足明周公之無罪而坐觀成王之疑，此則二公之心亦有猜于周公也。

translations.literal: Moreover when the Duke of Zhou undertook affairs he announced them to the Two Dukes; the Two Dukes were sufficient to show the Duke's innocence yet sat watching King Cheng's doubts — this shows the Two Dukes' hearts also harbored suspicion of the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke acted he reported to the Two Dukes; they could have proved his innocence yet sat watching the king's doubts — their hearts too suspected the Duke.

sentences.zh: 但以疏不間親，故寄言于管、蔡，可謂忠不見於當時，仁不及于兄弟。

translations.literal: But because the distant may not come between the close, they therefore lodged their words in Guan and Cai — one may say loyalty was not seen in that age and benevolence did not reach to brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Because the distant may not come between kin, they lodged their words in Guan and Cai — loyalty was unseen in that age and benevolence never reached his brothers.

sentences.zh: 知群望之有歸，天命之不在己，然後返政成王，以為忠耳。

translations.literal: Knowing that the multitude's allegiance had a destination and Heaven's mandate was not on himself, only then did he return power to King Cheng — this is what is called loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the people's allegiance had found its object and Heaven's mandate was not his, only then did he return power to King Cheng — and this they call loyalty.

sentences.zh: 大風拔木之征，乃皇天祐存周道，不忘文、武之德，是以赦周公之始愆，欲成周室之大美。

translations.literal: The omen of the great wind uprooting trees was Heaven's blessing to preserve the Zhou Way, not forgetting the virtue of Wen and Wu; therefore it pardoned the Duke of Zhou's initial fault and wished to complete the great beauty of the Zhou house.
translations.idiomatic: The great wind that uprooted trees was Heaven blessing the Zhou Way and remembering the virtue of Wen and Wu; it pardoned the Duke of Zhou's first fault to complete the Zhou house's glory.

sentences.zh: 考周公之心，原周公之行，乃天下之罪 人，何至德之謂也！

translations.literal: Examining the Duke of Zhou's heart and tracing the Duke of Zhou's conduct, he was a criminal under Heaven — how can one speak of utmost virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the Duke of Zhou's heart and trace his deeds — he was a criminal under Heaven; how can one call this utmost virtue!

sentences.zh: 周公復位，二公所以杜口不言其本心者，以明管、蔡之忠也。」

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou returned to power, the reason the Two Dukes sealed their lips and did not speak their true hearts was to make clear the loyalty of Guan and Cai."
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke returned to power, the Two Dukes kept silent about their true thoughts to show that Guan and Cai had been loyal."

sentences.zh: 又謂常忠曰：「伊尹、周公孰賢？

translations.literal: He also said to Chang Zhong: "Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou — which is the more worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Chang Zhong: "Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou — which was the greater man?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「伊尹非有周公之親而功濟一代，太甲亂德，放于桐宮，思愆改善，然後復之。

translations.literal: " Zhong said: "Yi Yin did not have the Duke of Zhou's kinship yet his merit aided a generation; when King Taijia's virtue was in disorder he was placed in the Tong Palace; when he reflected on his faults and improved, he was then restored."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong said: "Yi Yin lacked the Duke of Zhou's kinship yet his merit sustained an age; when King Taijia's conduct turned vicious he was confined in the Tong Palace until the king repented and was restored."

sentences.zh: 使主無怨言，臣無流謗，道存社稷，美溢來今，臣謂伊尹之勳有高周旦。

translations.literal: He made the sovereign without complaint and ministers without slander spreading; the Way was preserved in the altars of state and beauty overflowed to the present day — your subject holds that Yi Yin's achievement towers above Zhou Dan."
translations.idiomatic: He left the sovereign without grievance and ministers without scandal; the altars endured and his fame shines to this day — I hold Yi Yin's achievement above the Duke of Zhou's."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「伊尹以舊臣之重，顯阿衡之任，太甲嗣位，君道未洽，不能竭忠輔導。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Yi Yin with the weight of an old minister and the conspicuous charge of Chief Minister — when Taijia succeeded, the way of the ruler was not yet harmonized and he could not exhaust loyalty in guidance."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "Yi Yin bore the weight of an old minister and the open charge of Chief Minister; when Taijia succeeded the kingly Way was not yet settled and he failed to guide him with full loyalty."

sentences.zh: 而放黜桐宮，事同夷羿，何周公之可擬乎！

translations.literal: Yet he deposed him to the Tong Palace — the affair is the same as Yi of Xia — how can the Duke of Zhou be compared!"
translations.idiomatic: Instead he deposed him to the Tong Palace — the same as Yi of Xia — how can he be compared to the Duke of Zhou!"

sentences.zh: 」郎敷曰：「伊尹處人臣之位，不能匡制其君，恐成、湯之道墜而莫就，是以居之桐宮，與小人從事，使知稼穡之艱難，然後返之天位，此其忠也。

translations.literal: " Lang Fu said: "Yi Yin occupied the position of minister yet could not correct and restrain his ruler, fearing that the Way of Cheng and Tang would fall and not be attained; therefore he dwelt in the Tong Palace and associated with petty men, making him know the hardship of sowing and reaping, and then returned him to Heaven's throne — this was his loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: " Lang Fu said: "Yi Yin held a minister's post yet could not correct his ruler, fearing the Way of Cheng and Tang would be lost; he kept Taijia in the Tong Palace among common men until he knew the hardship of the fields, then restored him — that was loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「伊尹能廢而立之，何不能輔之以至於善乎？

translations.literal: " Sheng said: "If Yi Yin could depose and install him, why could he not assist him to goodness?"
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng said: "If Yi Yin could depose and restore him, why could he not guide him to virtue?"

sentences.zh: 若太甲性同桀紂，則三載之間未應便成賢後，如其性本休明，義心易發，當務盡匡規之理以弼成君德，安有人臣幽主而據其位哉！

translations.literal: If Taijia's nature were the same as Jie and Zhou, then within three years he should not suddenly have become a worthy successor; if his nature were originally bright and his righteous heart easy to awaken, he should have devoted himself to the principle of correcting and guiding to assist in completing the ruler's virtue — how can a minister imprison his lord and occupy his place!
translations.idiomatic: If Taijia were like Jie or Zhou, three years would not have made him virtuous; if his nature were sound and his heart easily moved to righteousness, Yi Yin should have guided him to complete virtue — how can a minister imprison his lord and hold his throne!

sentences.zh: 且臣之事君，惟力是視，奈何挾智藏仁以成君惡！

translations.literal: Moreover a minister serves his ruler only as strength allows — how can he harbor wisdom and hide benevolence to complete the ruler's wickedness!
translations.idiomatic: A minister serves his ruler with all his strength — how can he hoard wisdom and hide kindness to complete his lord's wickedness!

sentences.zh: 夫太甲之事，朕已鑒之矣。

translations.literal: As for the affair of Taijia, I have already judged it.
translations.idiomatic: I have already judged the affair of Taijia.

sentences.zh: 太甲，至賢之主也，以伊尹曆奉三朝，績無異稱，將失顯祖委授之功，故匿其日月之明，受伊尹之黜，所以濟其忠貞之美。

translations.literal: Taijia was a supremely worthy sovereign; because Yi Yin had served three reigns without distinctive praise, he would lose the achievement entrusted by his illustrious ancestor; therefore he hid the brightness of sun and moon and accepted Yi Yin's deposition — thus to complete the beauty of loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Taijia was a supremely worthy king; Yi Yin served three reigns without equal fame and risked losing his illustrious ancestor's trust, so he hid the king's brilliance and accepted deposition — thus completing the beauty of loyal integrity.

sentences.zh: 夫非常之人，然後能立非常之事，非常人之所見也，亦猶太伯之三讓，人無德而稱焉。

translations.literal: Only an extraordinary man can then establish an extraordinary affair — what an extraordinary man sees is also like Taibo's three yieldings, which men without virtue praised.
