translations.idiomatic: Only an extraordinary man can accomplish an extraordinary deed — what such men see is like Taibo's three yieldings, praised by men without true understanding.

sentences.zh: 」敷曰：「太伯三以天下讓，至仲尼而後顯其至德。

translations.literal: " Fu said: "Taibo thrice yielded All under Heaven; only after Confucius did his utmost virtue appear."
translations.idiomatic: " Fu said: "Taibo thrice yielded the realm; only Confucius revealed his utmost virtue."

sentences.zh: 太甲受謗於天下，遭陛下乃申其美。

translations.literal: Taijia was slandered by All under Heaven; it was only upon encountering Your Majesty that his beauty was declared."
translations.idiomatic: Taijia was slandered throughout the realm; only before Your Majesty is his virtue proclaimed."

sentences.zh: 」因而談宴賦詩，賜金帛各有差。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they conversed at leisure, composed poems, and bestowed gold and silk each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: " They then feasted, composed poems, and bestowed gold and silk according to rank.

sentences.zh: 遼西太守李郎在郡十年，威制境內，盛疑之，累征不赴。

translations.literal: Li Lang, Governor of Liaoxi, had held his command ten years and awed the realm within his borders; Sheng suspected him and repeatedly summoned him, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lang, Governor of Liaoxi, had governed ten years with iron control of his province; Sheng grew suspicious and summoned him repeatedly, but he refused to come.

sentences.zh: 以母在龍城，未敢顯叛，乃陰引魏軍，將為自安之計，因表請發兵以距寇。

translations.literal: Because his mother was in Longcheng he did not dare openly rebel; he secretly drew in the Wei army as a plan for his own security and therefore memorialized requesting troops to resist the invaders.
translations.idiomatic: His mother remained in Longcheng, so he dared not rebel openly; he secretly invited Wei forces for his own security and memorialized requesting troops to resist invasion.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「此必詐也。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "This must be a fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "This must be a ruse."

sentences.zh: 」召其使而詰之，果驗，盡滅其族，遣輔國將軍李旱率騎討之。

translations.literal: He summoned his envoy and interrogated him; it was verified as expected; he exterminated his entire clan and sent the Supporting State General Li Han with cavalry to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the envoy and questioned him; the fraud was confirmed; he exterminated Lang's clan and sent the Supporting State General Li Han with cavalry against him.

sentences.zh: 師次建安，召旱旋師。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jian'an; Sheng recalled Han to turn the army back.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jian'an; Sheng ordered Han to turn back.

sentences.zh: 朗聞其家被誅也，擁三千餘戶以自固。

translations.literal: When Lang heard his family had been executed, he gathered more than three thousand households to fortify himself.
translations.idiomatic: Learning his family had been executed, Lang gathered more than three thousand households to fortify himself.

sentences.zh: 及聞旱中路而還，謂有內變，不復為備，留其子養守令支，躬迎魏師于北平。

translations.literal: When he heard Han was returning midway, he thought there was internal turmoil and no longer made preparations; he left his son Yang to hold Lingzhi and went in person to welcome the Wei army at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Han was turning back, he thought rebellion had broken out within and relaxed his guard; he left his son Yang at Lingzhi and went in person to welcome the Wei army at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 旱候知之，襲克令支，遣廣威孟廣平率騎追朗，及於無終，斬之。

translations.literal: Han, having anticipated this, struck and took Lingzhi, sent the Broad Prestige Meng Guangping with cavalry to pursue Lang, overtook him at Wuzhong, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Han had foreseen this, seized Lingzhi, sent Meng Guangping with cavalry after Lang, caught him at Wuzhong, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 初，盛之追旱還也，群臣莫知其故。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sheng recalled Han, none of the ministers knew the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng first recalled Han, none of the ministers knew why.

sentences.zh: 旱既斬朗，盛謂群臣曰：「前以追旱還者，正為此耳。

translations.literal: After Han had beheaded Lang, Sheng said to the ministers: "The reason I earlier recalled Han was precisely for this."
translations.idiomatic: After Han killed Lang, Sheng told the ministers: "I recalled Han for precisely this reason."

sentences.zh: 朗新為叛逆，必忌官威，一則鳩合同類，劫掠良善，二則亡竄山澤，未可卒平，故非意而還，以盈怠其志，卒然掩之，必克之理也。

translations.literal: Lang had newly rebelled and was sure to fear official authority — on one hand he would gather like kinds and plunder the good, on the other he would flee into mountains and marshes and could not quickly be pacified; therefore I returned contrary to expectation to fill his will with ease, then suddenly struck him — the principle of certain victory."
translations.idiomatic: Lang had just rebelled and would fear official power — he would either rally allies and plunder the innocent or flee into the hills, impossible to crush at once; so I recalled Han unexpectedly to lull him, then struck suddenly — the sure path to victory."

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆曰：「非所及也。」

translations.literal: " The ministers all said: "Beyond what we could reach."
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers all said: "Beyond our foresight."

sentences.zh: 李旱自遼西還，聞盛殺其將衛雙，懼，棄軍奔走。

translations.literal: When Li Han returned from Liaoxi he heard Sheng had killed his general Wei Shuang; in fear he abandoned the army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Han returned from Liaoxi he learned Sheng had killed his general Wei Shuang; terrified, he abandoned the army and fled.

sentences.zh: 既而歸罪，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Presently he returned to acknowledge guilt and his rank and title were restored.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to acknowledge guilt and his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 盛謂侍中孫勍曰：「旱總三軍之任，荷專征之重，不能杖節死綏，無故逃亡，考之軍正，不赦之罪也。

translations.literal: Sheng said to the Attendant Grandee Sun Qin: "Han bore the charge of the three armies and the weight of independent command; he could not hold the staff and die at his post but fled without cause — judged by military law, it is a crime that may not be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng told the Attendant Grandee Sun Qin: "Han commanded the three armies and bore independent command; he could not die at his post but fled without cause — by military law this is unpardonable."

sentences.zh: 然當先帝之避難，眾情離貳，骨肉忘其親，股肱失忠節，旱以刑餘之體，效力盡命，忠款之至，精貫白日。

translations.literal: Yet when the Former Emperor was in flight and hardship, hearts were divided and kin forgot their parents, arms and legs lost loyal constancy — Han with the body of one punished by mutilation exerted his strength to the end of life; the utmost of loyal sincerity penetrated the white sun."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Former Emperor fled in hardship, kin turned traitor and loyal arms failed — Han, though mutilated in body, gave his life to the end; loyalty bright as the noon sun."

sentences.zh: 朕故錄其忘身之功，免其丘山之罪耳。」

translations.literal: I therefore record his merit of forgetting self and remit his crime as great as a mountain."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore record his merit of self-sacrifice and remit his mountain-sized crime."

sentences.zh: 盛去皇帝之號，稱庶人大王。

translations.literal: Sheng removed the title of emperor and styled himself the Great King, a common man.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng laid aside the imperial title and styled himself Great King, a commoner in name.

sentences.zh: 魏襲幽州，執刺史盧溥而去。

translations.literal: Wei raided You Province and seized the Inspector Lu Pu and took him away.
translations.idiomatic: Wei raided You Province, seized Inspector Lu Pu, and carried him off.

sentences.zh: 遣孟廣平援之，無及。

translations.literal: He sent Meng Guangping to rescue him, but it was too late.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Meng Guangping to rescue him, but arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 盛率眾三萬伐高句驪，襲其新城、南蘇，皆克之，散其積聚，徙其五千餘戶於遼西。

translations.literal: Sheng led thirty thousand to campaign against Koguryŏ, struck their Xincheng and Nansu, took both, dispersed their stores, and moved more than five thousand households to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng led thirty thousand against Koguryŏ, took Xincheng and Nansu, dispersed their stores, and moved more than five thousand households to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 盛引見百遼於東堂，考詳器藝，超拔者十有二人。

translations.literal: Sheng summoned and received the hundred Liao at the Eastern Hall, examined their talents and arts in detail, and elevated twelve who surpassed the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng received a hundred Liao officers in the Eastern Hall, examined their talents, and elevated twelve who stood above the rest.

sentences.zh: 命百司舉文武之士才堪佐世者各一人。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred offices each to recommend one civil or military gentleman whose talent could assist the age.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every office to recommend one civil or military man fit to serve the age.

sentences.zh: 立其子遼西公定為太子，大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: He installed his son, Duke of Liaoxi Ding, as crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty below the grade of capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son, the Duke of Liaoxi Ding, crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty short of capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 宴其群臣於新昌殿，盛曰：「諸卿各言其志，朕將覽之。

translations.literal: He feasted his ministers in Xinchang Hall; Sheng said: "Each of you, speak your ambition — I shall review them."
translations.idiomatic: He feasted his ministers in Xinchang Hall and said: "Speak your ambitions — I shall hear them."

sentences.zh: 」七兵尚書丁信年十五，盛之舅子也，進曰：「在上不驕，高而不危，臣之願也。

translations.literal: " The Master of the Seven Arms Ding Xin was fifteen years old, Sheng's nephew by a sister; he advanced and said: "Not arrogant though on high, lofty yet not in peril — this is your subject's wish."
translations.idiomatic: " The Master of the Seven Arms Ding Xin, fifteen and Sheng's nephew, stepped forward: "To be high yet not arrogant, lofty yet not in peril — that is my wish."

sentences.zh: 」盛笑曰：「丁尚書年少，安得長者之言乎！

translations.literal: " Sheng laughed and said: "Director Ding is young — how does he speak the words of an elder!"
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng laughed: "Director Ding is young — how does he speak like an elder!"

sentences.zh: 」盛以威嚴馭下，驕暴少親，多所猜忌，故信言及之。

translations.literal: " Sheng governed his subordinates with stern authority, was arrogant and violent and seldom intimate, and suspected many — therefore Xin's words touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng ruled with stern authority, was proud and violent and seldom close to others, and suspected much — hence Xin's words.

sentences.zh: 盛討庫莫奚，大虜獲而還。

translations.literal: Sheng campaigned against the Kumo Xi and returned with great captives.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng campaigned against the Kumo Xi and returned with great spoils.

sentences.zh: 左將軍慕容國與殿中將軍秦輿、段贊等謀率禁兵襲盛，事覺，誅之，死者五百餘人。

translations.literal: The Left General Murong Guo with the Palace Gentlemen Qin Yu, Duan Zan, and others plotted to lead the palace guard in a surprise strike against Sheng; the affair was discovered and they were executed — more than five hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: The Left General Murong Guo with Palace Gentlemen Qin Yu, Duan Zan, and others plotted to strike Sheng with the palace guard; discovered, they were executed — more than five hundred died.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、思悔侯段璣、輿子興、贊子泰等，因眾心動搖，夜於禁中鼓躁大呼。

translations.literal: The Forward General, Marquis of Sihui Duan Ji, Yu's son Xing, and Zan's son Tai — because hearts were shaken — by night within the palace beat drums, raised a clamor, and shouted.
translations.idiomatic: The Forward General Duan Ji, Xing son of Yu, and Tai son of Zan — exploiting shaken morale — drummed and shouted within the palace by night.

sentences.zh: 盛聞變，率左右出戰，眾皆披潰。

translations.literal: When Sheng heard of the disturbance he led his attendants out to fight; the host all broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the disturbance, Sheng led his guards out to fight; the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 俄而有一賊從暗中擊傷盛，遂輦升前殿，申約禁衛，召叔父河間公熙屬以後事。

translations.literal: Presently one bandit struck Sheng from hiding and wounded him; he was then carried up to the front hall, tightened the palace guard, summoned his uncle the Duke of Hejian Xi, and entrusted the later affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel struck him from hiding and wounded him; he was carried to the front hall, tightened the guard, summoned his uncle the Duke of Hejian Murong Xi, and entrusted the succession.

sentences.zh: 熙未至而盛死，時年二十九，在位三年。

translations.literal: Xi had not yet arrived when Sheng died; he was twenty-nine years old and had reigned three years.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had not yet arrived when Sheng died; he was twenty-nine and had reigned three years.

sentences.zh: 偽諡昭武皇帝，墓號興平陵，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Emperor Zhaowu; his tomb was called Xingping Mausoleum; his temple name was Zhong Zong.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu; his tomb was Xingping Mausoleum; his temple name Zhong Zong.

sentences.zh: 盛幼而羈賤流漂，長則遭家多難，夷險安危，備嘗之矣。

translations.literal: Sheng in youth was bound and cast adrift in hardship; grown, he met the family's many calamities; ease and peril, safety and danger — he tasted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng in youth knew bondage and exile; grown, he met the family's many calamities — ease and peril, safety and danger, he tasted them all.

sentences.zh: 懲寶暗而不斷，遂峻機威刑，織芥之嫌，莫不裁之於未萌，防之於未兆。

translations.literal: Punishing Bao's dimness and indecision, he thereupon made stern authority and punishment severe; the slightest grudge was cut off in the bud and guarded against before it appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by Bao's blindness and indecision, he sharpened authority and law; the slightest grudge was cut off before it sprouted.

sentences.zh: 於是上下振局，人不自安，雖忠誠親戚亦皆離貳，舊臣靡不夷滅，安忍無親，所以卒於不免。

translations.literal: Thereupon above and below trembled; men could not be at ease; though kinsmen were loyal they all turned away, old ministers were none not destroyed — cruel and without kin, therefore in the end he could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Court and realm trembled; none were at ease; loyal kin turned away and old ministers were destroyed — pitiless toward kin, and so he could not escape his end.

sentences.zh: 是歲隆安五年也。

translations.literal: This was the fifth year of Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fifth year of the Long'an era.

sentences.zh: 熙字道文，垂之少子也。

translations.literal: Xi, courtesy name Daowen, was Chui's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, whose courtesy name was Daowen, was Murong Chui's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 初封河間王。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 段速骨之難，諸王多被其害，熙素為高陽王崇所親愛，故得免焉。

translations.literal: In Duan Sugu's calamity many princes were harmed; Xi had always been loved by the Prince of Gaoyang Chong and therefore escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In Duan Sugu's uprising many princes perished; Xi was beloved by the Prince of Gaoyang Murong Chong and so survived.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗之篡也，以熙為遼東公，備宗祀之義。

translations.literal: In Lan Han's usurpation he made Xi Duke of Liaodong to fulfill the meaning of maintaining the ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Han usurped the throne he made Xi Duke of Liaodong to preserve the ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 盛初即位，降爵為公，拜都督中外諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射，領中領軍。

translations.literal: When Sheng first took the throne he reduced Xi's rank to duke and appointed him Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, Cavalry General-in-Chief, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and concurrently Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng first took power he reduced Xi to duke and appointed him Commander-in-Chief, Cavalry General-in-Chief, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 從征高句驪、契丹，皆勇冠諸將。

translations.literal: Following campaigns against Koguryŏ and the Khitan, his courage led all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigns against Koguryŏ and the Khitan his courage surpassed every general's.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「叔父雄果英壯，有世祖之風，但弘略不如耳。」

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Uncle is heroic, bold, and valiant, with the wind of Shizu — only his broad strategy is not equal."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "Uncle is heroic and bold, with the spirit of our founder — only his grand strategy falls short."

sentences.zh: 及盛死，其太后丁氏以國多難，宜立長君。

translations.literal: When Sheng died, the Empress Dowager Ding, because the state had many hardships, held that a mature ruler should be established.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng died, Empress Dowager Ding, considering the state's many hardships, argued a mature ruler should be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 群望皆在平原西元，而丁氏意在於熙，遂廢太子定，迎熙入宮。

translations.literal: The multitude's hope was all on Yuan of Pingyuan West, but the Ding clan's heart was set on Xi; they thereupon deposed the crown prince Ding and welcomed Xi into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Popular hope rested on Yuan of Pingyuan West, but Lady Ding favored Xi; they deposed Crown Prince Ding and welcomed Xi to the palace.

sentences.zh: 群臣勸進，熙以讓元，元固以讓熙，熙遂僭即尊位。

translations.literal: The ministers urged him to advance; Xi yielded to Yuan, Yuan firmly yielded to Xi, and Xi presumptuously assumed the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers urged him forward; Xi yielded to Yuan, Yuan firmly yielded back, and Xi took the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 誅其大臣段璣、秦興等，並夷三族。

translations.literal: He executed his great ministers Duan Ji, Qin Xing, and others, and exterminated their three clans.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the great ministers Duan Ji, Qin Xing, and others and exterminated their clans to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 元以嫌疑賜死。

translations.literal: Yuan was compelled to death on suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was forced to die on suspicion.

sentences.zh: 元字道光，寶之第四子也。

translations.literal: Yuan, courtesy name Daoguang, was Bao's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, whose courtesy name was Daoguang, was Bao's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 赦殊死已下，改元曰光始，改北燕台為大單于台，置左右輔，位次尚書。

translations.literal: He amnestied below the grade of capital offense, changed the reign title to Guangshi, changed the Northern Yan Terrace to the Grand Chanyu Terrace, and established Left and Right Assistants with rank below the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied short of capital crimes, changed the reign title to Guangshi, renamed the Northern Yan Terrace the Grand Chanyu Terrace, and established Left and Right Assistants ranking below the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 初，熙烝于丁氏，故為所立。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi had taken the Empress Dowager Ding as consort and was therefore installed by her.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xi had taken Empress Dowager Ding as consort and was enthroned through her favor.

sentences.zh: 及寵倖苻貴人，丁氏怨恚呪詛，與兄子七兵尚書信謀廢熙。

translations.literal: When he doted on the Honored Lady of the Fu clan, the Ding clan resented and cursed; with her nephew the Master of the Seven Arms Xin she plotted to depose Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When he favored Lady Fu, Lady Ding cursed him in resentment; with her nephew the Master of the Seven Arms Xin she plotted to depose him.

sentences.zh: 熙聞之，大怒，逼丁氏令自殺，葬以後禮，誅丁信。

translations.literal: When Xi heard of it he was greatly angered, compelled the Ding clan to kill herself, buried her with the rites due a consort, and executed Ding Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Xi in fury forced Lady Ding to kill herself, buried her with consort's rites, and executed Ding Xin.

sentences.zh: 熙狩于北原，石城令高和殺司隸校尉張顯，閉門距熙。

translations.literal: Xi hunted on the northern plain; the Magistrate of Shicheng Gao He killed the Director of the Masters of Writing Zhang Xian and shut the gates to bar Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi hunted on the northern plain; the Magistrate of Shicheng Gao He killed Director Zhang Xian and shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 熙率騎馳返，和眾皆投杖，熙入誅之。

translations.literal: Xi led horsemen in flight back; He's host all cast aside their staffs; Xi entered and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi galloped back; He's men threw down their weapons; Xi entered and executed him.

sentences.zh: 於是引見州郡及單于八部耆舊於東宮，問以疾苦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned the provincial and commandery officials and the elders of the eight tribes of the Chanyu to the Eastern Palace and asked after their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned provincial officials and the elders of the eight Chanyu tribes to the Eastern Palace and asked after their hardships.

sentences.zh: 大築龍騰苑，廣袤十餘里，役徒二萬人。

translations.literal: He greatly built Longteng Garden, more than ten li in breadth and length, with twenty thousand laborers.
translations.idiomatic: He built Longteng Garden on a vast scale — more than ten li across — with twenty thousand laborers.

sentences.zh: 起景雲山于苑內，基廣五百步，峰高十七丈。

translations.literal: He raised Jingyun Mountain within the garden, its base five hundred paces broad and its peak seventeen zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Within the garden he raised Jingyun Mountain, five hundred paces at the base and seventeen zhang high.

sentences.zh: 又起逍遙宮、甘露殿，連房數百，觀閣相交。

translations.literal: He also raised Xiaoyao Palace and Ganlu Hall, with hundreds of connected chambers and intersecting towers and pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: He also built Xiaoyao Palace and Ganlu Hall — hundreds of linked chambers with towers and galleries intertwined.

sentences.zh: 鑿天河渠，引水入宮。

translations.literal: He cut the Heavenly River canal to draw water into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He cut the Heavenly River canal to bring water into the palace.

sentences.zh: 又為其昭儀苻氏鑿曲光海、清涼池。

translations.literal: He also for his Lady of Complete Brightness of the Fu clan cut Quguang Sea and Qingliang Pool.
translations.idiomatic: For his Lady of Complete Brightness of the Fu clan he also excavated Quguang Sea and Qingliang Pool.

sentences.zh: 季夏盛暑，士卒不得休息，暍死者太半。

translations.literal: In the height of summer the soldiers could not rest; more than half died of heatstroke.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer the laborers could not rest; more than half died of heatstroke.

sentences.zh: 熙游于城南，止大柳樹下，若有人呼曰：「大王且止。

translations.literal: Xi roamed south of the city and halted beneath a great willow; it was as if someone called: "Great King, halt for a moment."
translations.idiomatic: Xi roamed south of the city and stopped under a great willow; a voice seemed to call: "Great King, wait."

sentences.zh: 」熙惡之，伐其樹，乃有蛇長丈餘，從樹中而出。

translations.literal: " Xi hated it, cut down the tree, and thereupon a serpent more than a zhang long came out from within the tree.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi in disgust cut down the tree, and a serpent more than ten feet long emerged from its trunk.

sentences.zh: 立其貴嬪苻氏為皇后，赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: He installed his Honored Lady of the Fu clan as empress and amnestied below the grade of capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: He made his Honored Lady of the Fu clan empress and declared an amnesty short of capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 熙北襲契丹，大破之。

translations.literal: Xi raided the Khitan in the north and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xi raided the Khitan in the north and routed them.

sentences.zh: 昭儀苻氏死，偽諡湣皇后。

translations.literal: When the Lady of Complete Brightness of the Fu clan died, her posthumous title was Empress Min.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Fu died, her posthumous title was Empress Min.

sentences.zh: 贈苻謨太宰，諡文獻公。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored Fu Mo as Grand Preceptor with the title Duke of Literature and Presentation.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored Fu Mo as Grand Preceptor, Duke of Literature and Presentation.

sentences.zh: 二苻並美而豔，好微行遊宴，熙弗之禁也。

translations.literal: Both Fu ladies were beautiful and seductive, fond of going out incognito on pleasure excursions; Xi did not forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: Both Fu ladies were beautiful and seductive and loved secret outings; Xi did not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 請謁必從，刑賞大政無不由之。

translations.literal: For audiences and petitions he always followed; great matters of punishment and reward were none not through them.
translations.idiomatic: They attended every audience and petition; punishments and great policies all passed through them.

sentences.zh: 初，昭儀有疾，龍城人王溫稱能療之，未幾而卒，熙忿其妄也，立於公車門支解溫而焚之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Lady of Complete Brightness was ill, the Longcheng man Wang Wen claimed he could cure her; before long she died; Xi resented his falsehood, stood him at the public carriage gate, dismembered him limb from limb, and burned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Fu fell ill, the Longcheng man Wang Wen claimed he could cure her; she soon died; Xi, furious at the fraud, had him dismembered at the public gate and burned.

sentences.zh: 其後好游田，熙從之，北登白鹿山，東過青嶺，南臨滄海，百姓苦之，士卒為豺狼所害及凍死者五千餘人矣。

translations.literal: Afterward he loved hunting excursions; Xi followed him; he ascended Bailu Mountain in the north, passed Qing Ridge in the east, and faced the blue sea in the south — the common people suffered bitterly; soldiers harmed by wolves and jackals and those who died of freezing numbered more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He then loved the hunt; Xi followed; north to Bailu Mountain, east past Qing Ridge, south to the sea — the people suffered; more than five thousand soldiers fell to beasts or frost.

sentences.zh: 會高句驪寇燕郡，殺略百餘人。

translations.literal: Then Koguryŏ raided Yan Commandery and killed and carried off more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ then raided Yan Commandery, killing and capturing more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 熙伐高句驪，以苻氏從，為沖車地道以攻遼東。

translations.literal: Xi campaigned against Koguryŏ; the Fu clan followed; he made assault towers and underground passages to attack Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi campaigned against Koguryŏ with Lady Fu in train, building assault towers and tunnels against Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「待剗平寇城，朕當與後乘輦而入，不聽將士先登。

translations.literal: Xi said: "Wait until we level the rebel city — I shall enter with the consort in the imperial carriage and will not allow the officers and soldiers to mount first."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "When the rebel city is level I shall enter with the consort in the imperial carriage — the troops shall not mount the walls before us."

sentences.zh: 」於是城內嚴備，攻之不能下。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the city made strict preparations within; the attack could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: " The city made strict defense; the assault failed.

sentences.zh: 會大雨雪，士卒多死，乃引歸。

translations.literal: Then great wind and snow came; many soldiers died; he thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard struck; many soldiers died; he turned the army homeward.

sentences.zh: 擬鄴之鳳陽門，作弘光門，累級三層。

translations.literal: Patterning himself on Ye's Fengyang Gate, he made the Hongguang Gate with three tiers of steps.
translations.idiomatic: Modeling Ye's Fengyang Gate, he built the Hongguang Gate in three tiers.

sentences.zh: 熙與苻氏襲契丹，憚其眾盛，將還，苻氏弗聽，遂棄輜重，輕襲高句驪，周行三千餘里，士馬疲凍，死者屬路。

translations.literal: Xi with the Fu clan raided the Khitan; fearing their great numbers, he was about to return, but the Fu clan would not listen; he thereupon abandoned baggage and lightly struck Koguryŏ, circling more than three thousand li — horses and men exhausted and frozen, the dead lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: Xi raided the Khitan with Lady Fu; fearing their numbers he turned back, but she refused; abandoning baggage he struck Koguryŏ lightly, marching three thousand li — men and horses exhausted and frozen, the dead heaped along the road.

sentences.zh: 攻木底城，不克而還。

translations.literal: He attacked Mudi city, could not take it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Mudi city, failed to take it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 盡殺寶諸子。

translations.literal: He executed all of Bao's sons.
translations.idiomatic: He executed all of Bao's sons.

sentences.zh: 大城肥如及宿軍，以仇尼倪為鎮東大將軍、營州刺史，鎮宿軍，上庸公懿為鎮西將軍、幽州刺史，鎮令支；

translations.literal: The great city of Feiru and Sujun — he made Chou Ni Ni Grand General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying Province to garrison Sujun, and Duke of Shangyong Yi Grand General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of You Province to garrison Lingzhi;
translations.idiomatic: At the great city of Feiru and Sujun he appointed Chou Ni Ni Grand General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying Province at Sujun, and the Duke of Shangyong Yi Grand General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of You Province at Lingzhi;

sentences.zh: 尚書劉木為鎮南大將軍、冀州刺史，鎮肥如。

translations.literal: the Master of Writing Liu Mu Grand General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Ji Province to garrison Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: and the Master of Writing Liu Mu Grand General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Ji Province at Feiru.

sentences.zh: 為苻氏起承華殿，高承光一倍，負土於北門，土與穀同價。

translations.literal: He raised Chenghua Hall for the Fu clan, twice the height of Chengguang, and carried earth at the northern gate until earth was the same price as grain.
translations.idiomatic: He built Chenghua Hall for Lady Fu, twice the height of Chengguang, and heaped earth at the northern gate until soil cost as much as grain.

sentences.zh: 典軍杜靜載棺詣闕，上書極諫。

translations.literal: The Commandant Du Jing carried a coffin to the gate and memorialized with extreme remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant Du Jing brought a coffin to the gate and memorialized in the strongest remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 熙大怒，斬之。

translations.literal: Xi was greatly angered and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi in rage beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 苻氏嘗季夏思凍魚膾，仲冬須生地黃，皆下有司切責，不得，加以大辟，其虐也如此。

translations.literal: The Fu clan once in midsummer desired frozen fish slices, in mid-winter desired fresh rehmannia — orders went down to the offices with stern blame, and when they could not obtain them capital punishment was added; his cruelty was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu once wanted frozen fish in midsummer and fresh rehmannia in midwinter — offices were harshly charged, and failure brought death; such was his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 苻氏死，熙悲號躃踴，若喪考妣，擁其屍而撫之曰：「體已就冷，命遂斷矣！

translations.literal: When the Fu clan died, Xi wailed and stamped as if mourning father and mother, embraced her corpse and stroked it, saying: "The body is already cold, life is cut off!"
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Fu died, Xi wailed and stamped as for parents, embraced her corpse and said: "The body is cold — life is ended!"

sentences.zh: 」於是僵僕氣絕，久而乃蘇。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he stiffened and his breath stopped; after a long while he revived.
translations.idiomatic: " He stiffened and ceased breathing; long afterward he revived.

sentences.zh: 大斂既訖，復啟其棺而與交接。

translations.literal: After the great encoffinment was finished, he again opened the coffin and coupled with her.
translations.idiomatic: After the encoffinment he opened the coffin again and lay with her.

sentences.zh: 服斬縗，食粥。

translations.literal: He wore unhemmed sackcloth and ate gruel.
translations.idiomatic: He wore coarse mourning and ate only gruel.

sentences.zh: 制百僚于宮內哭臨，令沙門素服。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to mourn within the palace; he ordered Buddhist monks to wear plain robes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials to mourn within the palace and monks to wear plain robes.

sentences.zh: 使有司案檢哭者，有淚以為忠孝，無則罪之，於是群臣震懼，莫不含辛以為淚焉。

translations.literal: He had the offices investigate the mourners: those with tears were deemed loyal and filial, those without were punished — the ministers all trembled and none failed to hold bitterness to make tears.
translations.idiomatic: He had mourners inspected: tears meant loyalty, dry eyes meant punishment — ministers trembled and forced tears with clenched grief.

sentences.zh: 慕容隆妻張氏，熙之嫂也，美姿容，有巧思。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Murong Long, was Xi's sister-in-law, beautiful in bearing and clever in design.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, wife of Murong Long and Xi's sister-in-law, was beautiful and clever in design.

sentences.zh: 熙將以為苻氏之殉，欲以罪殺之，乃毀其禭靴，中有弊氈，遂賜死。

translations.literal: Xi intended to make her follow the Fu clan in death and wished to kill her on a charge; he destroyed her burial boots — inside were worn felt — and thereupon granted her death.
translations.idiomatic: Xi meant to sacrifice her with Lady Fu and sought a charge to kill her; he ruined her burial boots, found worn felt inside, and sentenced her to death.

sentences.zh: 三女叩頭求哀，熙不許。

translations.literal: Her three daughters knocked their heads and begged for mercy; Xi would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Her three daughters begged on their knees; Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 制公卿已下至於百姓，率戶營墓，費殫府藏。

translations.literal: He ordered the dukes and ministers down to the common people, household by household, to build tombs, exhausting the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every household from nobles to commoners to build tombs, draining the treasury.

sentences.zh: 下錮三泉，周輸數里，內則圖畫尚書八坐之象。

translations.literal: He sank three springs, the perimeter several li; within were painted the images of the Eight Seats of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He dug three springs over several li, painting within the Eight Seats of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「善為之，朕將隨後入此陵。

translations.literal: Xi said: "Do it well — I shall follow afterward into this mound."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "Do it well — I shall enter this mound after."

sentences.zh: 」識者以為不祥。

translations.literal: " Observers held it inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " Observers called it ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 其右僕射韋璆等並懼為殉，沐浴而待死焉。

translations.literal: The Right Vice Director Wei Qiu and others all feared being sacrificed and bathed awaiting death.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Vice Director Wei Qiu and others feared sacrifice and bathed awaiting death.

sentences.zh: 號苻氏墓曰征平陵。

translations.literal: He titled the Fu clan's tomb Zhengping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lady Fu's tomb Zhengping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 熙被髮徒跣，步從苻氏喪。

translations.literal: Xi with loose hair and bare feet walked following the Fu clan's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Xi with hair loose and feet bare walked behind Lady Fu's bier.

sentences.zh: 轜車高大，毀北門而出。

translations.literal: The funeral carriage was huge and tall; it destroyed the northern gate in passing out.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral carriage was immense; it smashed the northern gate on the way out.

sentences.zh: 長老竊相謂曰：「慕容氏自毀其門，將不久也。」

translations.literal: The elders whispered to one another: "The Murong clan destroys its own gate — they will not last long."
translations.idiomatic: Elders whispered: "The Murongs destroy their own gate — they will not endure."

sentences.zh: 中衛將軍馮跋、左衛將軍張興，先皆坐事亡奔，以熙政之虐也，與跋從兄萬泥等二十二人結盟，推慕容雲為主，發尚方徒五千餘人閉門距守。

translations.literal: The Central Guard General Feng Ba and the Left Guard General Zhang Xing, who had earlier been punished and fled, because Xi's government was cruel joined with Ba's cousin Wan Ni and twenty-two others in alliance, pushed Murong Yun as leader, and raised more than five thousand convict artisans of the Imperial Workshop to shut the gates and resist.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba and Zhang Xing, earlier punished and fled, judged Xi's rule cruel; with Ba's cousin Wan Ni and twenty-two others they allied, made Murong Yun leader, and rallied five thousand Imperial Workshop convicts to shut the gates and resist.

sentences.zh: 中黃門趙洛生奔告之，熙曰：「此鼠盜耳，朕還當誅之。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Zhao Luosheng ran to report; Xi said: "These are rat bandits — when I return I shall execute them."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant Zhao Luosheng reported; Xi said: "Rat thieves — I shall kill them when I return."

sentences.zh: 」乃收發貫甲，馳還赴難。

translations.literal: " He thereupon gathered armor, donned it, and galloped back to meet the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: " He donned armor and galloped back.

sentences.zh: 夜至龍城，攻北門不克，遂敗，走入龍騰宛，微服隱于林中，為人所執，雲得而弑之，及其諸子同殯城北。

translations.literal: By night he reached Longcheng, attacked the northern gate without success, was defeated, fled into Longteng Garden, went in plain dress to hide in the woods, was seized by men, Yun got him and assassinated him, and buried him with his sons together north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: By night he reached Longcheng, failed at the northern gate, fled to Longteng Garden, hid in the woods in disguise, was seized, and Yun killed him and buried him with his sons north of the city.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三，在位六年。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three years old and had reigned six years.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-three and had reigned six years.

sentences.zh: 雲葬之於苻氏墓，偽諡昭文皇帝。

translations.literal: Yun buried him at the Fu clan's tomb with the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Yun buried him beside Lady Fu with the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowen.

sentences.zh: 垂以孝武帝太元八年僭立，至熙四世，凡二十四年，以安帝義熙三年滅。

translations.literal: Chui presumptuously established himself in the eighth year of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin's Taiyuan era; to Xi was four generations, altogether twenty-four years; in the third year of Emperor An's Yixi era it perished.
translations.idiomatic: Chui seized power in the eighth year of Taiyuan; through Xi was the fourth generation — twenty-four years in all — and in the third year of Yixi it fell.

sentences.zh: 初，童謠曰：「一束槁，兩頭然，禿頭小兒來滅燕。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's song said: "A bundle of stalk, both ends burning, a bald-headed boy comes to destroy Yan."
translations.idiomatic: A children's song had said: "A bundle of stalk, both ends burning — a bald-headed boy comes to destroy Yan."

sentences.zh: 」槁字上有草，下有禾，兩頭然則禾草俱盡而成高字。

translations.literal: " The character gao has grass above and grain below; both ends burning then grain and grass are both exhausted and form the character gao.
translations.idiomatic: " The character gao has grass above and grain below; both ends burning leaves grain and grass consumed — forming gao.

sentences.zh: 雲父名拔，小字禿頭，三子，而雲季也。

translations.literal: Yun's father was named Ba, childhood name Bald Head; of three sons Yun was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's father was named Ba, childhood name Bald Head; of three sons Yun was youngest.

sentences.zh: 熙竟為雲所滅，如謠言焉。

translations.literal: Xi in the end was destroyed by Yun, as the song said.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was destroyed by Yun, as the song foretold.

sentences.zh: 慕容雲，字子雨，寶之養子也。

translations.literal: Murong Yun, courtesy name Ziyu, was Bao's adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yun, whose courtesy name was Ziyu, was Bao's adopted son.

sentences.zh: 祖父和，高句驪之支庶，自雲高陽氏之苗裔，故以高為氏焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather He was a collateral branch of Koguryŏ; Yun himself claimed descent from the Gaoyang clan and therefore took Gao as surname.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He was of Koguryŏ collateral stock; Yun claimed Gaoyang descent and took Gao as surname.

sentences.zh: 雲沈深有局量，厚重希言，時人咸以為愚，唯馮跋奇其志度而友之。

translations.literal: Yun was deep and reserved with breadth of measure, heavy and seldom speaking; contemporaries all thought him foolish — only Feng Ba marveled at his ambition and breadth and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was deep, reserved, and sparing of speech; most thought him dull — only Feng Ba saw his ambition and befriended him.

sentences.zh: 寶之為太子，雲以武藝給事侍東宮，拜侍御郎，襲敗慕容會軍。

translations.literal: When Bao was heir apparent, Yun by martial arts served in attendance at the Eastern Palace, was appointed Attendant Gentleman, and defeated Murong Hui's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao was heir apparent, Yun served the Eastern Palace by martial skill, was made Attendant Gentleman, and routed Murong Hui's army.

sentences.zh: 寶子之，賜姓慕容氏，封夕陽公。

translations.literal: Bao made him his son, granted the surname Murong, and enfeoffed him Duke of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao adopted him, granted the Murong surname, and enfeoffed him Duke of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 熙之葬苻氏也，馮跋詣雲，告之以謀。

translations.literal: When Xi was burying the Fu clan, Feng Ba went to Yun and told him the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi buried Lady Fu, Feng Ba came to Yun with the plot.

sentences.zh: 雲懼曰：「吾嬰疾歷年，卿等所知，願更圖之。

translations.literal: Yun in fear said: "I have been ill for years — you know this; pray find another plan."
translations.idiomatic: Yun in fear said: "I have been ill for years, as you know — choose another leader."

sentences.zh: 」跋逼曰：「慕容氏世衰，河間虐暴，惑妖淫之女而逆亂天常，百姓不堪其害，思亂者十室九焉，此天亡之時也。

translations.literal: " Ba pressed him: "The Murong house declines generation by generation; the Prince of Hejian is cruel and violent, bewitched by demonic licentious women and perverting Heaven's constant way — the common people cannot bear the harm; nine in ten households think of rebellion — this is the time Heaven destroys them."
translations.idiomatic: " Ba pressed: "The Murongs decline; the Prince of Hejian is cruel, led astray by a witch and perverting Heaven's way — the people cannot endure it; nine in ten think of rebellion — Heaven's hour has come."

sentences.zh: 公自高氏名家，何能為他養子！

translations.literal: You are of a famous house of the Gao clan — how can you be another man's adopted son!
translations.idiomatic: You are of the great Gao house — how can you remain another's adopted son!

sentences.zh: 機運難邀，千歲一時，公焉得辭也！

translations.literal: Opportunity is hard to invite — a thousand years, one moment — how can you decline!
translations.idiomatic: Fortune comes once in a thousand years — how can you refuse!

sentences.zh: 」扶之而出。

translations.literal: " They supported him and brought him out.
translations.idiomatic: " They raised him up and led him out.

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「吾疾苦日久，廢絕世務。

translations.literal: Yun said: "My illness has long been severe and I have abandoned worldly affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said: "My illness is long and I have left worldly affairs."

sentences.zh: 卿今興建大事，謬見推逼。

translations.literal: You now raise a great affair and wrongly push and compel me.
translations.idiomatic: You raise a great affair and wrongly force me.

sentences.zh: 所以徘徊，非為身也，實惟否德不足以濟元元故耳。

translations.literal: The reason I hesitate is not for myself — truly my virtue is insufficient to rescue the people.
translations.idiomatic: I hesitate not for myself — my virtue is too slight to save the people.

sentences.zh: 」跋等強之，雲遂即天王位，復姓高氏，大赦境內殊死以下，改元曰正始，國號大燕。

translations.literal: " Ba and the others pressed him; Yun thereupon assumed the title of Heavenly King, resumed the Gao surname, proclaimed a general amnesty within the realm below capital offense, changed the reign title to Zhengshi, and the state name Great Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " They pressed him; Yun took the title Heavenly King, resumed the surname Gao, declared amnesty short of capital crimes, adopted the reign title Zhengshi, and named the state Great Yan.

sentences.zh: 署馮跋侍中、都督中外諸軍事、征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、錄尚書事、武邑公，封伯、子、男，鄉、亭侯者五十餘人，士卒賜穀帛有差。

translations.literal: He appointed Feng Ba Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, Grand General Who Campaigns North, Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Wuyi; he enfeoffed more than fifty as marquises, earls, and viscounts of counties and townships; soldiers received grain and cloth each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Feng Ba Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief, Grand General Who Campaigns North, Grand Marshal equal to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Duke of Wuyi; he enfeoffed more than fifty marquises and earls; soldiers received grain and cloth by rank.

sentences.zh: 熙之群官，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Xi's host of officials — their ranks and titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's officials had their ranks restored.

sentences.zh: 立妻李氏為天王後，子彭為太子。

translations.literal: He installed his wife Lady Li as Heavenly Queen and his son Peng as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He made his wife Lady Li Heavenly Queen and his son Peng crown prince.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉慕輿良謀叛，雲誅之。

translations.literal: The Rapid Cavalry Commandant Murong Liang plotted rebellion; Yun executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Rapid Cavalry Commandant Murong Liang plotted rebellion; Yun executed him.

sentences.zh: 雲臨東堂，幸臣離班、桃仁懷劍執紙而入，稱有所啟，拔劍擊雲，雲以幾距班，桃仁進而弑之。

translations.literal: Yun was at the Eastern Hall; his favored minister Li Ban and Taoren concealed swords, entered with paper claiming something to report, drew swords and struck Yun; Yun blocked Ban with a table; Taoren advanced and assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Hall, favored minister Li Ban and Taoren entered with swords hidden in papers, struck Yun — he blocked Ban with a table — and Taoren killed him.

sentences.zh: 馮跋遷雲屍於東宮，偽諡惠懿皇帝。

translations.literal: Feng Ba moved Yun's corpse to the Eastern Palace with the posthumous title Emperor Huiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba moved Yun's body to the Eastern Palace with the posthumous title Emperor Huiyi.

sentences.zh: 雲自以無功德而為豪桀所推，常內懷懼，故寵養壯士以為腹心。

translations.literal: Yun, considering himself without merit yet pushed by the bold, always harbored fear within; therefore he favored and maintained stalwarts as his vitals.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, knowing he lacked merit yet was pushed forward by the bold, lived in constant fear and kept stalwarts as his inner guard.

sentences.zh: 離班、桃仁等並專典禁衛，委之以爪牙之任，賞賜月至數千萬，衣食臥起皆與之同，終以此致敗雲。

translations.literal: Li Ban, Taoren, and others exclusively held the palace guard, were entrusted with the tasks of claws and teeth, monthly rewards reaching tens of millions; in food, clothing, rising and sleeping they were all the same as he — in the end through this they brought about Yun's ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban, Taoren, and others held the palace guard alone, trusted as his claws and teeth, rewarded by the tens of millions monthly, sharing his food and bed — and through this ruined him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：四星東聚，金陵之氣已分；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Four stars gathered in the east — the aura of Jinling was already divided;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Four stars gathered in the east — Jinling's destiny was already divided;

sentences.zh: 五馬南浮，玉塞之雄方擾。

translations.literal: five horses floated south — the strength of the jade barrier was just then in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: five horses drifted south — the north's strength was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 市朝屢改，艱虞靡息。

translations.literal: Markets and courts changed repeatedly; hardship and peril never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Courts and markets shifted endlessly; hardship never ceased.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂天資英傑，威震本朝，以雄略見猜而庇身寬政，永固受之而以禮，道明事之而畢力。

translations.literal: Murong Chui by Heaven's gift was an heroic outstanding man, awe-inspiring to his dynasty; because his bold strategy was suspected he sheltered himself under a lenient regime; Yonggu firmly received him with ritual; Daoming served him and exhausted his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui was Heaven-touched, heroic, and awe-inspiring; suspected for his bold strategy he sheltered under a lenient master; Fu Jian received him with ritual; he served Fu Jian with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 然而隼質難羈，狼心自野。

translations.literal: Yet the falcon's nature is hard to bind; the wolf's heart is wild by birth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a falcon's nature cannot be tethered; a wolf's heart is wild from birth.

sentences.zh: 淮南失律，三甥之謀已構；

translations.literal: At Huainan he lost discipline — the three nephews' plot was already formed;
translations.idiomatic: At Huainan discipline failed — the three nephews' plot took shape;

sentences.zh: 河朔分麾，五木之祥雲啟。

translations.literal: on the north of the River banners divided — the auspicious clouds of the Five Mulberries opened.
translations.idiomatic: north of the Yellow River banners divided — the omen of the Five Mulberries rose.

sentences.zh: 斬飛龍而遐舉，逾石門而長邁，遂使翟氏景從，鄴師宵逸，收羅趙、魏，驅駕英雄。

translations.literal: He cut down the flying dragon and soared afar, crossed Shimen and marched long — thereupon the Di clan followed in his train, the Ye army fled by night; he gathered Zhao and Wei and drove the heroes.
translations.idiomatic: He struck down the flying dragon and soared away, crossed Shimen and marched on — the Di followed, the Ye army fled by night; he gathered Zhao and Wei and drove the heroes.

sentences.zh: 叩囊餘奇，摧五萬于河曲；

translations.literal: Tapping the bag's remaining wonders, he crushed fifty thousand at the river bend;
translations.idiomatic: From the bag's last wonders he crushed fifty thousand at the river bend;

sentences.zh: 浮船秘策，招七郡于黎陽。

translations.literal: with secret plans on floating boats he recruited seven commanderies at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: with secret plans on floating boats he drew seven commanderies at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 返遼陰之舊物，創中山之新社，類帝禋宗，僭擬斯備。

translations.literal: He recovered the old possessions of Liaoyin and founded the new community of Zhongshan; imitating the Emperor's suburban rites, usurpation was complete.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Liaoyin's old lands and founded Zhongshan anew; imitating imperial rites, usurpation was complete.

sentences.zh: 夫以重耳歸晉，賴五臣之功；

translations.literal: When Chong'er returned to Jin, he relied on the merit of five ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er returned to Jin on the merit of five ministers;

sentences.zh: 句踐紿吳，資五千之卒。

translations.literal: Goujian deceived Wu with five thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian deceived Wu with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 惡有業殊二霸，眾微一旅，掎拔而傾山嶽，騰嘯而禦風雲！

translations.literal: How could there be achievement unlike the two hegemons, a host slight as one brigade, prying to topple mountains and roaring to ride the wind and clouds!
translations.idiomatic: How could achievement rival the two hegemons come from a single slight brigade, prying mountains aside and roaring at wind and cloud!

sentences.zh: 雖衛人忘亡復傳于東國，任好余裕伊愧於西鄰，信苻氏之奸回，非晉室之鯨鯢矣。

translations.literal: Though Wey's men forgot extinction yet the transmission continued in the eastern state; Duke Mu's surplus made Yi ashamed before the western neighbor — truly the Fu clan's treacherous villainy, not the Jin house's whale and kraken.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wey forgot ruin yet lived on in the east; Duke Mu's surplus shamed Yi in the west — truly the Fu clan's treachery, not the Jin house's ruin.

sentences.zh: 寶以浮譽獲升，峻文禦俗，蕭牆內憤，勍敵外陵，雖毒不被物而惡足自剿。

translations.literal: Bao by floating reputation obtained advancement, stern texts to control the custom; inner fury within the palace walls, fierce enemies pressing from without — though poison did not touch things, enough wickedness to destroy himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rose on empty reputation, ruled by harsh law; fury within, fierce foes without — though his poison did not touch all, wickedness enough to destroy himself.

sentences.zh: 盛則孝友冥符，文武不墜，韜光而夷仇賊，罪己而遜高危，翩翩然濁世之佳虜矣。

translations.literal: Sheng then had filial piety and friendship in dark accord, civil and martial not fallen; he hid his light and pacified enemy and bandit, blamed himself and yielded high peril — gracefully the fine captive of a turbid age.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng matched filial piety and friendship in secret, kept civil and martial from falling; he hid his light, pacified foes, blamed himself and yielded peril — a fine spirit in a turbid age.

sentences.zh: 熙乃地非奧主，舉因淫德。

translations.literal: Xi's land was not a hidden lord's; his rise came entirely through licentious virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was no hidden lord; his rise came entirely through licentious favor.

sentences.zh: 驪戎之態，取悅于匡床；

translations.literal: The posture of Li Rong pleased on the couch;
translations.idiomatic: Li Rong's charms pleased on the couch;

sentences.zh: 玄妻之姿，見奇於鬒發。

translations.literal: Xuan Qi's beauty was marvelled at in black hair.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Qi's beauty dazzled in dark hair.

sentences.zh: 蕩輕舟于曲光之海，望朝涉于景雲之山，飾土木於驕心，窮怨嗟於蕞壤，宗祀夷滅，為馮氏之驅除焉。

translations.literal: He floated light boats on the sea of Quguang, watched the morning ford from Jingyun Mountain, adorned earth and wood to feed arrogant hearts, exhausted lamentation on a tiny soil — the ancestral sacrifices were destroyed and he became the Fu clan's scourge.
translations.idiomatic: He floated light boats on Quguang's sea, watched dawn crossings from Jingyun Mountain, built earth and wood to feed pride, exhausted grief on a mote of soil — the ancestral rites perished and he became prey for the Feng clan.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：戎狄憑陵，山川沸騰。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The barbarians relied on force; mountains and rivers boiled.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Barbarians relied on force; mountains and rivers seethed.

sentences.zh: 天未悔禍，人非與能。

translations.literal: Heaven had not yet repented the calamity; men were not those who could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had not yet repented the calamity; no man could succeed.

sentences.zh: 疾走而捷，先鳴則興。

translations.literal: Run fast and you are swift; cry first and you rise.
translations.idiomatic: Run fast and you are swift; cry first and you rise.

sentences.zh: 道明烈烈，鞭笞豪傑。

translations.literal: Daoming blazing, whipping the bold heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming blazing, lashing the bold heroes.

sentences.zh: 掃燕夷魏，釗屠永滅。

translations.literal: Sweeping Yan, leveling Wei, striking Ju and Yong to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: He swept Yan, leveled Wei, struck Ju and Yong to extinction.

sentences.zh: 大盜潛移，鴻名遂竊。

translations.literal: The great robber moved in secret; the great name was stolen.
translations.idiomatic: The great thief moved in secret; the great name was stolen.

sentences.zh: 寶心生亂，盛清家難。

translations.literal: Bao's heart gave birth to disorder; Sheng cleared the family's peril.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's heart bred disorder; Sheng cleared the family peril.

sentences.zh: 熙極驕淫，人懷憤惋。

translations.literal: Xi reached the extreme of arrogant licentiousness; men harbored indignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: Xi reached arrogant debauchery's extreme; men nursed wrath.

sentences.zh: 孽貽身咎，災無以逭。

translations.literal: Crime bequeathed bodily calamity — disaster could not be escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Sin passed to the body — disaster could not be escaped.
